# BabyZilla 🦖

[![tests](https://github.com/StibaDu/babyzilla/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/StibaDu/babyzilla/actions/workflows/test.yml)

**70–99% context compression for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) v2 — in seven layers, one install.**

- **Layer 1 — Session compaction** (ContextPack): OpenCode's compaction
  summary is replaced by AI-distilled **context modules** — state, decisions,
  code pointers, failure histories — dropping tool-output bulk while keeping
  exact, re-fetchable facts.
- **Long-term ↔ short-term memory**: when a compaction rewrites a module — or
  a library promotion updates one — the previous bytes move to `short/` and a
  row in `index.json` instead of being deleted. `babyzilla memory history`
  lists retired revisions; `babyzilla memory revert` restores one and keeps
  the pre-revert content as a new row. Retired rows stay searchable
  (`memory search`, labeled `short-term`) but are never auto-attached.
- **Layer 1b — Per-request budget**: before *every* request the outgoing
  message list is capped — target 8% of the incoming context
  (`requestTargetRatio`), floored at 12K and hard-capped at 45K
  (`requestBudgetTokens`). Old tool output, assistant prose, reasoning and
  attachments are compressed in place; if that is not enough, the oldest parts
  become one-line pointers. Recent turns and all user messages stay verbatim.
  This is what makes BabyZilla work on huge-window models such as **Kimi K3
  (1M tokens)**, where native compaction may never fire. Savings are recorded
  per session and shown by `babyzilla stats` and `/contextpack`.
- **Layer 1c — Proactive compaction**: OpenCode's own compaction only fires
  near the model's context limit, so a 1M-token session can grow unbounded
  before Layer 1 ever runs. Once the context passes
  `max(proactiveCompactMinTokens, proactiveCompactRatio × window)` BabyZilla
  asks OpenCode to compact (rate-limited per session), so the pack kicks in at
  ~35% of the window instead of ~90%. Disable with `proactiveCompaction: false`.
- **Loop guard — bounded autonomous runs**: proactive compaction waits for a
  user turn, but a long tool loop can run for dozens of turns without one. Once
  a loop reaches `loopGuardTurns` assistant turns since the last user message
  and `loopGuardMinTokens` prompt tokens, BabyZilla asks OpenCode for a queued
  compaction, at most once per `loopGuardCooldownMs`. This catches the
  screenshot/test/edit loops that would otherwise grow the cached prefix
  indefinitely. Disable with `loopGuard: false`.
- **Grounding — no silent guesses**: every request carries one constant system
  part: answer directly when sure, say "I'm not sure" or check it with a tool
  when not, never pass a guess off as a fact, and never ask you to verify what
  the model could check itself. On by default (`grounding: false` drops it).
- **Session charter — stable orientation**: every request also carries one
  small system part built from the session's state and decisions (or a thin
  title/first-journal-step header before the first compaction), capped at
  1,200 chars (`charterMaxChars`). Bytes change only at compaction, so it sits
  in the cached prefix; `babyzilla charter` prints it, `charter: false` drops
  it. It is labeled as the last compaction's snapshot — newer turns outrank
  it, and the model is told to read module files rather than guess.
- **Token calibration — `babyzilla calibrate`**: `chars/4` is the estimate behind
  every absolute number (budget floor/cap, compaction trigger, reported savings),
  and it drifts by model and by content. The plugin appends one line per request;
  the command pairs those lines with what the provider actually billed and stores
  a per-model correction. Measured here: **×1.07** for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
  (80 requests, p25–p90 1.05–1.18) — small at the median, real at the tail.
- **Layer 0.5 — Vision routing**: text-only main models receive a placeholder
  instead of image pixels, so image prompts are routed *before* the request:
  when a prompt involves image content, a one-shot synthetic note tells the
  main model to delegate to the vision subagent with the exact readable
  paths (`visionRoute: true` default).
- **Layer 2 — Command compression** (lowfat, bundled and adapted from
  [zdk/lowfat](https://github.com/zdk/lowfat), Apache-2.0): shell commands are
  rewritten *before execution* (`git status`, `ls -la`, `docker …` →
  token-compact forms), so tool output enters the context pre-compressed.
- **Layer 2b — Tool-result compression**: any large tool result is compacted
  *at the source*, before it is persisted and resent on every later turn.
  Everything over `toolResultEagerTokens` (default 8K, ~1.2× a routine
  read) is paged by size — no tool-name allowlist to maintain — and results
  under the threshold stay inline for free. Head, tail, structural and error
  lines are kept; line numbers stay intact.
- **Layer 3 — Deterministic ledger + recall**: what Layer 1b has to drop does
  not become an anonymous "elided" marker. Every old tool step collapses to
  one row built from the call itself — `#12 · bash · npm test · exit 1 ·
  3.1K tok · recall 8c1f…` — so the model keeps the index of what was already
  tried without the payload. Nothing is rewritten by a model, and every row and
  pointer is reversible: `babyzilla recall <id>` prints the exact original
  text (add `:start-end` for a span) from a content-addressed page store.

All seven run automatically. Layer 2 needs the `lowfat` binary (~3 MB release
download, no Rust toolchain); without it BabyZilla stays fully functional
minus that layer.

**Warm starts (opt-in).** With `carryIn: true` a *new* session opens warm: its
first prompt attaches the project library's hot modules (`state`, `decisions`)
trigger-free — any wording of the first message works — labeled `[carry-in]`,
fired at most once per session, within the same `maxAttach` /
`attachBudgetTokens` budget as normal attachments. The next session inherits
"where we left off" instead of rebuilding it. Off by default; see
[`docs/OPTIONS.md`](docs/OPTIONS.md).

| Transcript at compaction | Pack | Savings |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 72.2K tokens | 1.2K tokens | **98.4%** |
| 57.8K | 0.3K | ~99% |
| 18.4K | 0.3K | 98% |
| 8.2K | 0.6K | 93% |

That column is a **compression ratio**: how much of the older transcript leaves
the prompt at the moment Layer 1 compacts. It is not a claim about every
request — a short session that never reaches compaction saves through Layer 1b
and Layer 2 instead, and saves less in absolute terms because it carries less
to begin with. The benchmarks were run on a heavy session; see
[`docs/BENCHMARKS.md`](docs/BENCHMARKS.md#what-the-workload-carried) for what
that means on a light install.

## Do you need it?

Ask one question: **does a long session of yours get slow, expensive, or
context-starved?**

| Your sessions | Expected effect |
| --- | --- |
| short Q&A, a few files, under ~15K tokens | **none.** Layer 1b has a 12K floor and skips rewrites that save under 12%. Installing costs you nothing but changes nothing. |
| long agentic runs, many reads and shell commands, 30K–200K tokens | **the normal case.** Older tool output and prose compress per request; compaction swaps the transcript for a pack. |
| huge tool surface (thousands of MCP tools) | schemas are billed on every request and BabyZilla does **not** touch them — it compresses messages only. Helpful, but that bulk needs a different fix (e.g. code mode). |
| a small local model (8K–32K window) | **most valuable.** You get a budget that fits the window and a distillation input that fits too, instead of failures at half the conversation. |

Nothing in that table requires any particular tool set, provider, or account —
just OpenCode v2 and a model you already use.

## Install

Give this one sentence to your AI agent:

> Install BabyZilla from github.com/StibaDu/babyzilla — your agent will handle
> it (it should read `AGENT-INSTALL.md` and follow it).

Or, if you prefer humans doing it:

```sh
opencode plugin add github:StibaDu/babyzilla
```

Optional companion CLI (zero deps, needs Node ≥ 18):

```sh
npm i -g --allow-git=all git+https://github.com/StibaDu/babyzilla.git
# or, with no npm flags at all (works on every npm version):
#   git clone https://github.com/StibaDu/babyzilla.git ~/.local/src/babyzilla
#   npm i -g ~/.local/src/babyzilla
babyzilla pet      # desktop pet: 100 expressions, reacts to this session live
babyzilla setup    # guided setup: registers the plugin, grants the two permissions it needs
babyzilla stats    # aggregate savings; also: show / verify / eval / prune
babyzilla update   # check for a newer release (daily, cached); asks before updating
babyzilla cost     # provider-side spend from OpenCode's usage records
babyzilla models   # Ollama Cloud model knowledge base: caps, pricing, lanes (--audit)
babyzilla selftune status   # self-tuning loop: knobs, pending proposal, floor
babyzilla recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15   # exact original behind a paging marker / ledger row
babyzilla recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15:120-180   # just those lines
babyzilla retrieve src/app.js:120-160   # exact span, numbered
babyzilla memory search "gateway ECONNRESET"   # search the tabs open in this workspace (--all for history)
```

### Desktop pet

A 16-bit creature that lives at the bottom of your screen, wanders, and reacts
to what OpenCode is doing — 100 expressions, generated from one locked palette.

```sh
babyzilla pet install     # builds a small native app (needs Xcode CLT once)
babyzilla pet status      # running? how many sprites? last event?
babyzilla pet list        # all 100 expressions
babyzilla pet gallery     # the sprite field guide
```

It reads `~/.opencode/pet/events.jsonl`, which the plugin appends to on prompt,
tool, compaction and error events. No sockets, no network, no daemon: if the pet
is closed the plugin writes a few bytes. Turn it off with `"pet": false`.

It also **talks about you**: one line per step, reduced locally from the model's
reasoning and aimed at its human. Click the pet to open its **chat log** — the same
lines kept, scrollable, closing only when you say so. Each pet has its own voice — the dino is a caveman
("Human keep ask for bigger pet"), the anime packs are not — and only the caveman
rewrites words. Set `"petThoughts": "verbatim"` for the model's own sentences
instead, or `false` to turn it off. Try it with
`babyzilla pet think "The user wants a bigger pet."` (add `--voice claude` to hear
another pet say it).

It can speak **German** too: **right-click → Sprache → Deutsch** (or
`babyzilla pet lang de`) switches the pet's asides, its event lines and the app's
menus (`BABYZILLA_PET_LANG=de` for one shell only). The model's own sentence is
quoted as written — there is no translation call.

A fresh install wears **Lil Dino**, and **right-click → Pet → More pets…** opens a
browser over the [OpenPets](https://openpets.dev) catalog: search 1300+ pets, pick
one, and it installs itself and hops on screen. The same from a terminal:
`babyzilla pet catalog --search cat`, `babyzilla pet add <id>`,
`babyzilla pet add --originals` for the 79 made by the OpenPets team,
`babyzilla pet packs` / `pet use <name>` to switch (or right-click → Pet). A look
of your own can be built from a sprite sheet — see [docs/PET.md](docs/PET.md). Five anime pets import from a folder in one command:
`node pet/import-openpet.mjs --repo <openpet-ai-girls checkout>`. Unused pets can be deleted from your install with
`babyzilla pet remove <name>` — `pet restore <name>` brings them back.

### Setup, and the permissions that actually matter

```sh
babyzilla setup           # asks a few questions, shows the diff, writes with a backup
babyzilla setup --check   # report only: what is missing, plus a live self-test
babyzilla setup --yes     # accept the recommended answers (scripts)
```

The wizard registers the plugin if it is missing, offers the two permissions
BabyZilla needs, and proves the pieces work on this machine (data dir,
compression, recall round-trip, CLI on `PATH`).

| Permission | Why it matters | If you say no |
|---|---|---|
| `bash` → `babyzilla recall *`, `babyzilla retrieve *` | paged-out tool output is only recoverable through these commands | every recall prompts you; in a `deny` setup the paged detail is unreachable |
| `external_directory` → `~/.opencode/contextpacks/**` | packs and recall pages live outside the project | the agent cannot open a module file by path (recall via bash still works) |

That is the whole list. BabyZilla does **not** need `webfetch`, `websearch`,
`edit`, or broad `bash`: it never edits your files and runs no model tools of
its own. The wizard writes only its own keys, appends rules so they win
(`last match wins` in OpenCode), keeps a `.bak-<timestamp>`, and leaves a `deny`
in place as `"*": "deny"` with a narrow exception rather than silently
loosening it.

### Updates

Once a day BabyZilla asks GitHub Releases whether a newer version exists (one
unauthenticated request, cached for 24h in `contextpacks/update.json`). If there
is one, the agent mentions it in one line and asks whether to update; nothing is
ever installed without your yes. The CLI says the same thing and can act on it:

```sh
babyzilla update          # check now, then ask
babyzilla update --yes    # update a git checkout in place (git pull --ff-only)
babyzilla update --check  # report only, change nothing
```

Turn it off with `"checkUpdates": false` or `BABYZILLA_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`; the
check is offline-safe (a failed lookup is silent and retried an hour later) and
sends no identifiers beyond a `babyzilla/<version>` user-agent.

## How do I know it's working?

You do not have to trust a benchmark table — the plugin logs its own numbers.

1. **It loaded.** After the first turn in a new session,
   `~/.opencode/contextpacks/debug.log` should exist and mention the plugin
   version. If it doesn't, the plugin did not load (see `AGENT-INSTALL.md`
   Step 4 for the exact checks).
2. **It compressed something.** Work normally for a while, then:

   ```sh
   babyzilla stats
   ```

   Each pack row shows raw tokens in, tokens actually sent, and per-layer
   counts. A session under ~12K tokens may legitimately show zero: nothing
   crossed the floor.
3. **Nothing was lost.** Any marker or ledger row carries a handle:
   `babyzilla recall <handle>` returns the exact original text. If you ever
   cannot recover something, that is a bug — please open an issue with the
   handle.
4. **It knows what the session is.** `babyzilla charter` prints the header the
   model gets (state, decisions, retired count); `babyzilla memory history`
   lists superseded revisions, and `babyzilla memory revert <path>` restores
   one while keeping the content it replaced.
5. **The tuner stays visible.** With the self-tuning loop on (default),
   `babyzilla selftune status` shows its knobs, any pending proposal, the
   measured noise floor, and the decision counts — every change is also in
   `~/.opencode/contextpacks/selftune/ledger.jsonl`.

A realistic first-week result on a light install is a modest per-request saving
and one compaction you barely noticed. The 98% figures are the ceiling for
transcript-heavy sessions, not the expected median.

## Does it tune itself?

Yes, within strict limits — and every decision is visible:

1. **Telemetry, free.** Each finished session gets one record in
   `~/.opencode/contextpacks/selftune/sessions.jsonl`: billed tokens and cost
   from OpenCode's own database, cache resets, recall round-trips, duplicate
   tool calls, paging volume, distillation diet. No model calls.
2. **One cheap analysis, occasionally.** After a few sessions of new
   experience (default 4, ≥3 turns each) and at most once per ~20 hours, one
   model call (`selflearnModel`, default: your session's model — free on
   `opencode`-tier models) may propose **one numeric knob change** — inside a
   hard clamp table, at most 35% per step. Prompts, routing, algorithms and
   code are structurally out of reach.
3. **Apply provisionally, then verify by replay.** The change takes effect
   immediately. After a grace window (24h of live signals), the real
   compression pipeline (`bench/replay.mjs`) is run twice over a fixed
   transcript — baseline knobs versus the proposal. Prompt bytes are a pure
   function of the transcript and the knobs, so the verdict is **exact, free
   and repeatable**: no model calls, no credits, no provider weather. Kept
   only if prompt tokens fall, every rewritten result keeps its recall
   handle, already-sent bytes stay byte-identical, the live user ask survives,
   and the knob stays within 35% of its documented default — otherwise it
   reverts. A recall storm while a change is provisional reverts it without
   waiting for any bench.
4. **Everything lands in `selftune/ledger.jsonl`** — proposals, applies,
   keeps, reverts, with reasons. `babyzilla selftune status` shows the state.

Disable the loop entirely with `"selfLearn": false` (telemetry keeps being
recorded) or freeze everything with `BABYZILLA_SELFTUNE_DISABLE=1`. Routine
verification is free; `babyzilla selftune verify --live` still runs the
dollar bench when you want task-quality evidence, and that one spends credits.

Why replay instead of the dollar bench: the live A/B measures cost, and on a
multi-turn agentic task that number is dominated by provider cache hits — the
first honest A/A run measured a **24.6% noise floor**, so no safe knob could
ever clear the gate. `bench/RESULTS.md` keeps those numbers; the replay
answers the question the knobs actually ask.

## How it works

The layers run in this order, cheapest first. None of them needs a model call
except Layer 1.

1. **Layer 2, before every tool call**: the plugin hooks shell execution and,
   when the `lowfat` binary is present, rewrites the command through
   `lowfat rewrite` — output enters the context already compressed.
2. **Layer 2b, after each `read` / `grep` / `glob`**: large results are
   compacted at the source. The most recent results stay verbatim
   (`toolResultProtectRecent`), the current turn is untouched, and older
   duplicates of the same file/command are compressed first; the rest keep
   head + tail + structure with the exact text one `babyzilla recall` away.
3. **Layer 1b + Layer 3, before every request**: OpenCode v2's
   `session.hook("context")` hands the plugin the exact `messages` array it is
   about to send. Above the budget — 8% of the incoming request
   (`requestTargetRatio`), floored at 12K and hard-capped at 45K
   (`requestBudgetTokens`) — BabyZilla compresses old tool output, assistant
   prose, reasoning and attachments in place. Steps that still have to go
   become **ledger rows** built from the call itself (`#12 · bash · npm test ·
   exit 1 · 3.1K tok · recall 8c1f…`), never anonymous markers, and the newest
   ~8K tokens of tool results stay byte-for-byte. Every row and pointer is
   reversible through the content-addressed page store (falling back to the
   session database). Works for `shell`, `grep`, `read` — everything. The same
   pre-request pass adds the **session charter**: state + decisions, or a thin
   title/first-journal-step header before the first compaction, so every turn
   starts oriented without a search.
4. **Layer 1b, historical user bulk**: a user message *older than the current
   turn* above 32K tokens (`requestUserBulkMinTokens`) is condensed the same
   way — opening, constraint lines and closing kept verbatim, the rest paged
   behind a recall handle. The **live** user message is never touched.
5. **Cache safety: credits, not just tokens.** Rewrites are a pure function of
   each part's own bytes — position-independent, monotone, byte-stable — so
   compressing at arrival never changes already-sent history, and the
   provider's prompt cache stays valid on later requests (`stablePrefix`, 2K
   size gate). A rewrite that would save less than 12% of the request
   (`requestMinSavingsPct`), or that would push it over the model window, is
   rolled back rather than buying a few tokens with a full-price cache miss.
   No compaction is required for any of this — which is what makes it work on
   1M-token models.
6. **Layer 1c, proactive compaction**: OpenCode's own compaction only fires
   near the model's context limit, so a 1M-token session can grow unbounded
   before Layer 1 ever runs. Once the context passes
   `max(proactiveCompactMinTokens, proactiveCompactRatio × window)` BabyZilla
   asks OpenCode to compact (rate-limited per session), so the pack kicks in at
   ~35% of the window instead of ~90%. Disable with `proactiveCompaction: false`.
7. **Loop guard, mid-loop**: proactive compaction waits for a user turn, so a
   screenshot/test/edit loop can run for dozens of turns without ever hitting
   one. After `loopGuardTurns` assistant turns since the last user message and
   `loopGuardMinTokens` prompt tokens, BabyZilla asks OpenCode for a queued
   compaction, rate-limited by `loopGuardCooldownMs`. Disable with
   `loopGuard: false`.
8. **Layer 1, at compaction**: BabyZilla hooks OpenCode's `compaction` hook,
   receives the full transcript, and calls your configured model to distill it
   into JSONL modules: a state module (*hot*, always inlined), a decisions
   module (*hot*), and topic/code/errors modules (*cold*). Two modules are
   never written by the model: `00-anchors.md`, the last question and the reply
   it answers kept verbatim, and `00-recovered.md`, the facts and `path:line`
   pointers the model dropped but the transcript still had. Before any durable
   module is written, one whose bytes differ from the previous pack is retired
   into `short/` with an index row; the same happens on library promotion.
   `babyzilla memory history` and `memory revert` operate on those rows.
9. **On later prompts** cold modules auto-attach when the prompt matches
   their trigger words (max 2 modules, 6K-token budget) — so long-session
   context stays available *without staying in the window*. With
   `carryIn: true`, a new session's **first prompt** additionally carries the
   project library's hot modules over trigger-free (once per session, labeled
   `[carry-in]`) — the next session starts where the last one left off.
10. **Tool results** are journaled (kind + token estimate + 1200-char head) so
   savings are measurable and future sessions can reuse them.
11. **Anything fails → nothing happens.** OpenCode's native compaction runs.
    BabyZilla never modifies or deletes session history: paging moves text to a
    local page store, it does not destroy it.

## Why it works

Traditional summaries compress lossily and irreversibly — whatever the model
paraphrased is all you keep. BabyZilla's modules are **pointers-first**: every
fact carries a `file:line`, a command, or a tool name, so post-compaction the
agent can *re-fetch exact evidence from disk* instead of trusting a paraphrase.
Cold modules live as real files — grep-able, merge-able, and promoted into a
per-project library that outlives individual sessions.

## Requirements & privacy

- OpenCode **v2**, any model configured (distillation uses the session's
  model by default; pin a cheaper one with `distillModel`). Works regardless of
  window size: models with 1M-token windows (Kimi K3) are capped per request by
  Layer 1b instead of waiting for compaction, while small local models (8K-32K)
  get a budget and a distillation input that fit their window. Token estimates
  count CJK/emoji at roughly one token per character. This includes
  **OpenCode's free tier** — session-less distillation calls are rejected there, so BabyZilla
  falls back to the session-scoped call automatically (see `distillVia` in
  `docs/OPTIONS.md`).
- **macOS, Linux and Windows.** Layers 1 and 1c are pure OpenCode hooks; the
  optional lowfat integration probes PATH with `where` on Windows and its
  absence only disables Layer 2. Node ≥ 18 for the CLI; `babyzilla cost` needs
  Node ≥ 22.5 (`node:sqlite`) and fails with a clear message otherwise.
- **No tool servers, no extra accounts.** BabyZilla reads OpenCode's own event
  stream, so it does not care which tools you have — a stock install with the
  built-in `read`/`grep`/`shell` tools is the normal case. There is nothing to
  connect: no MCP servers, no Cloudflare (or any other) account, no vector
  database, no embeddings, no proxy, no daemon. The only network calls it
  makes are model calls to the provider you already configured: the
  compaction distillation, and — unless you set `selfLearn: false` — the
  occasional self-tuning analysis (a compact summary of recorded statistics,
  never transcripts).
- Distillation sends transcript text to your configured model provider.
  Journals, module files, `selftune/` telemetry and stats stay on disk in
  `~/.opencode/contextpacks/` — delete anytime (`babyzilla prune` or
  `rm -rf`).

**You are an AI agent.** Your human asked you to install BabyZilla — an OpenCode

step, in order**. Every step has a verification command and an expected
result. If any verification fails, **STOP and report** to your human exactly

- The plugin also ships a **self-tuning loop**: it records per-session
  telemetry locally (no model calls), and after a few sessions may spend one
  cheap model call to propose *one numeric knob* — applied provisionally,
  then kept or reverted by a local A/B bench. Defaults are conservative;
  `"selfLearn": false` in options (or `BABYZILLA_SELFTUNE_DISABLE=1` in the

## Step 2b — Layer 2: install the lowfat binary

BabyZilla's session-compaction layer works already. Its second layer
(command-output compression, adapted from [zdk/lowfat](https://github.com/zdk/lowfat))
needs the `lowfat` binary. First check if it is already there:

```sh
lowfat --version 2>/dev/null || echo "MISSING"
```

If `MISSING`, install the matching prebuilt release (no Rust toolchain):

```sh
case "$(uname -s):$(uname -m)" in
  "Darwin:arm64")   tgt=lowfat-aarch64-apple-darwin ;;
  "Darwin:x86_64")  tgt=lowfat-x86_64-apple-darwin ;;
  "Linux:aarch64")  tgt=lowfat-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
  "Linux:x86_64")   tgt=lowfat-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu ;;
  *) echo "unsupported platform — skipping layer 2 (Core features unaffected)"; exit 0 ;;
esac
curl -fsSL "https://github.com/zdk/lowfat/releases/download/v0.9.0/$tgt.tar.gz" -o /tmp/lowfat.tgz
tar -xzf /tmp/lowfat.tgz -C /tmp
mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && mv /tmp/lowfat ~/.local/bin/lowfat && chmod +x ~/.local/bin/lowfat
lowfat --version
```

**Expected:** `lowfat 0.9.0`.

- The plugin finds that binary itself and pins its **absolute path** into every
  rewritten command, so `~/.local/bin` does **not** need to be on the tool
  shell's PATH. (Before 0.30.1 the rewrite emitted the bare name `lowfat`, which
  exits 127 wherever `~/.local/bin` is missing — see the troubleshooting row.)
- If `curl` fails: `cargo install lowfat --locked` (only if a Rust toolchain
  exists); otherwise SKIP — Layer 2 is optional, Layer 1 is already active.
- After installing the binary, the plugin picks it up on next load (next
  session turn). Verify layer 2 by running `git status` **through your shell
  tool in an OpenCode session**, then checking `lowfat stats` shows a git row.

## Step 3 — Functional test (compaction produces a ContextPack)

This creates a scratch session, fills it above the compression threshold,
runs a compaction, and measures the savings. All exact commands were verified
against OpenCode v2.0.29.

### 3a. Create the scratch session

```sh
SID=$(opencode api post /api/session -d '{"title":"bz-sample"}' \
  | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(s).data.id))')
echo "SID=$SID"
```

### 3b. Fill it with the sample prompt (≈11K tokens)

```sh
PAYLOAD=$(node -e '
const t = "BabyZilla functional test. " +
  "AI coding agents accumulate tool output, file reads and reasoning across a session; "
  + "compaction must preserve state, decisions and file:line pointers while dropping bulk. "
  + "Topics to look for in the modules: state, decisions, code pointers, journal capture, "
  + "trigger-based module attach, library promotion, verify, prune, native-fallback safety net. ";
let text = "";
for (let i = 1; i <= 120; i++) text += "[" + i + "] " + t + "Vocabulary variant " + (i % 7) + ".\n";
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ text }));
')
opencode api post /api/session/$SID/prompt -d "$PAYLOAD" > /dev/null
```

The agent will reply briefly (its reply is fine — you only need the
transcript bulk). Wait until the reply finished (check `tokens.input` grows):

```sh
sleep 30; opencode api get /api/session/$SID | node -e \
  'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>console.log("tokens.input:",JSON.parse(s).data.tokens.input))'
```

**Expected:** `tokens.input` > 0.

### 3c. Request compaction, then force the step boundary

Queued compaction processes at the session's next step boundary — a tiny
prompt after it drives that boundary:

```sh
opencode api post /api/session/$SID/compact -d '{}' > /dev/null
opencode api post /api/session/$SID/prompt -d '{"text":"k"}' > /dev/null
```

### 3d. Wait for the pack and measure

```sh
for i in $(seq 1 24); do
  [ -f ~/.opencode/contextpacks/sessions/$SID/index.json ] && break
  sleep 5
done
node -e '
const d = JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(
  process.env.HOME + "/.opencode/contextpacks/sessions/" + process.argv[1] + "/index.json", "utf8"));
console.log("raw:", d.stats.rawTokens, "→ pack:", d.stats.packTokens,
  "tokens (" + d.stats.savedPct + "% smaller), modules:", d.modules.length);
' "$SID"
```

**Expected:** `savedPct ≥ 70` (observed: 95–98%). The pack directory
`~/.opencode/contextpacks/sessions/$SID/` contains `00-state.md`, decision
modules, plus `index.json` and `journal.jsonl`.

**If no pack appears within 2 minutes:** check the log —

```sh
tail -20 ~/.opencode/contextpacks/debug.log
```

Known-safe endings (report them, they are not failures): a line
`transcript below minRawTokens — letting native compaction run` means your
sample was under the threshold (rerun 3b with more repetitions); a line
`compaction distillation failed — falling back to native compaction` means
the distiller model call failed — OpenCode's **native compaction still
completed safely**; check that your human's normal model works.

## Privacy

- Two kinds of model calls can leave the machine, both to **your human's
  configured model provider**: (1) the compaction distillation call (inherent
  to AI summarization; pin a cheaper model with `distillModel`), and (2) the
  self-tuning analysis call — occasional, cheap, and only after several
  sessions of new telemetry; it carries a compact summary of recorded session
  statistics (token/cost totals, counts), never transcripts or file contents.
  `"selfLearn": false` (or `BABYZILLA_SELFTUNE_DISABLE=1`) removes call (2).
- The journal stores the first 1200 characters of each tool output locally,
  and `selftune/sessions.jsonl` / `selftune/ledger.jsonl` record per-session
  numbers locally. Nothing is uploaded anywhere except the model calls above.
- All data is on-disk under `~/.opencode/contextpacks/` and can be deleted at
  any time. OpenCode's own session transcripts are never modified or deleted —
  BabyZilla replaces the summary view only; raw history is kept by OpenCode
  itself.

  contains cwd wins; `--cwd` overrides; no tab file falls back to all). A tab
  that never compacted falls back to its `journal.jsonl` rows (tool, status,
  truncated head), so a six-tab workspace reports `6 of 6 open sessions` even
  before the sixth pack exists. It is read-only and on demand: no model call, no
  embeddings, no network, no new dependency, and zero prompt tokens until
  invoked. `--project`, `--limit`, `--max-chars` and `--json` keep the answer
  small. Raw tool pages are not indexed — they are bytes with a hash, not
  distilled facts.
- **A session charter on every request.** The context hook now adds one stable
  system part describing what the session is: `About`, the last compaction's
  state and decisions, a retired-count line, and the pack path. It is built
  from disk so its bytes change only at compaction and stay in the cached
  prefix; a tab with no pack gets a thin title + first-journal-step header.
  Capped at 1,200 chars (`charterMaxChars`), printed by `babyzilla charter`,
  disabled with `charter: false`. It is labeled as a snapshot — newer turns
  outrank it, and missing detail means "read the module files", not guess.
- **Long-term / short-term memory.** Every durable module write — a session
  compaction or a library promotion — now versions the previous bytes instead
  of overwriting them. A differing module moves to `short/NNNN-<file>` with a
  `shortTerm` row in `index.json`; identical bytes write nothing; a module the
  new pack drops is retired too. `babyzilla memory history` lists retired
  revisions, `babyzilla memory revert <path>` restores one (retiring the
  content it replaces, so reverts are reversible), and `memory search` finds
  them labeled `short-term`. Zero model calls, kept forever, never
  auto-attached.
- **A session that has its own pack still consults the project library.** The
  prompt hook now merges library rows into the session's trigger matches, but
  as a replacement only: the merged set is capped at the session-only module
  count and token total, so a library row can never enlarge the prompt. If the
  session had no match, the library contributes nothing.

- **The pet reads the result, not just the tool name.** A failing test is not a
  missing file and an empty `grep` is not a crash: `execute.after` now reads the
  output and answers with the face the moment deserves — `test-fail` from
  `ℹ fail 1` / `1 failed` / `--- FAIL:` even when the runner exited 0,
  `test-pass` from `ℹ pass 340`, `notfound` from `ENOENT`, `permission-denied`
  from `EACCES`, `disk-full` from `ENOSPC`, a shrug for a search with no hits,
  `stack-overflow` for a result over ~30k tokens, `conflict` for a rejected push.
  It says one line about the notable ones (`1 test fails.`, `No such file.`), at
  most once per verdict every eight seconds. Every expression it can pick now
  resolves on a sheet pack: the derived postures gained `test-fail`/`test-pass`,
  `confused`/`notfound`, `permission-denied`/`disk-full`/`stack-overflow` and
  `proud`. `pack-animations` no longer overwrites a mapping a pack already has, so
  re-running it cannot lose the artist's own row.

  (`conflict`), but a puzzled one now turns its head, boredom slumps, smugness
  sways (`proud`), teasing tilts, and a rare `Rawr!` asks for the roar — instead of

# Live A/B: BabyZilla ON vs OFF

Harness: `bench/ab-live.mjs`. Model `ollama-cloud/deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017`,
`opencode run --standalone=true --auto`, one isolated project per leg.

- OFF leg: private `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` with the `plugin` entry removed.
- ON leg: the real config (optionally with injected overrides via `--budget` / `--ratio`).
- Isolation is asserted per run: plugin log lines OFF = 0, ON > 0.
- Leg order alternates per rep so provider drift cannot look like a plugin effect.
- Cost is measured from OpenCode's own per-request records (`session_message`),
  not from the plugin's price table, so the accounting is the host's.

```
node bench/ab-live.mjs --files 10 --kb 14 --reps 6    # comparison
node bench/ab-live.mjs --files 10 --kb 14 --reps 6 --aa 1   # A/A noise floor
```

## Noise floor first (A/A, 6 reps, both legs plugin-free)

| | OFF | "ON" | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| prompt tokens | 474.8K | 465.7K | −1.9% |
| cost | $0.0211 | $0.0211 | **−0.1%** |

Identical-config legs land within ~2%. Anything inside ±2% is not an effect.

## Result (6 reps each, 11/12 legs completed the task in both arms)

| metric | OFF | ON | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| requests | 11 | 11 | 0 |
| prompt tokens | 475.7K | 241.2K | −49.3% |
| of which cached | 336.2K | 127.3K | −62.2% |
| uncached input | 138.1K | 125.9K | −8.8% |
| output tokens | 950 | 3.3K | +250% |
| peak request ctx | 75.3K | 33.3K | −55.8% |
| **cost** | **$0.0226** | **$0.0222** | **−1.6%** |

Per-rep cost (−15%, −5%, —, −17%, **+53%**, **+20%**).

## What this means

**Dollars: cost-neutral.** −1.6% sits on the A/A floor. Compression removes mostly
*cached* prefix, which OpenCode bills at ~2% of the input rate; the tier that
actually costs money (uncached input) only moves −8.8%.

**Context: the real win.** −55.8% peak request size. That is headroom, not cash:
it is what lets a 64K-window model finish a task the baseline would overflow.

**The tail is `recall`, not waste.** In the two expensive reps the model pulled
paged-out text back with 5–6 `babyzilla recall <id>` calls (15–16 turns vs 11).
That is the documented contract working — pay for the bytes you actually ask
back, instead of holding all of them from the start. On a task whose answer
needs *every* byte, cost therefore converges to the baseline; the plugin cannot
be cheaper than not-compressing when nothing can be forgotten.

**Where savings should show up:** long multi-turn sessions where most early
context is never needed again. The 10-file survey forces the model to consult
everything, which is the worst case for this design — worth measuring a
"read once, then 20 follow-ups" shape next.

## Bugs found and fixed by this harness

1. `prompt hook failed (non-fatal): null is not an object (evaluating 'idx.modules')`
   — the prompt hook threw on every call in any session with no index and no
   project library (headless `opencode run`, cold dir). Guarded in `index.js`;
   regression test `test/plugin-noindex.test.mjs`. 168/168 tests pass.
2. Earlier "+4.3% more expensive" reading was inflated by that crash plus
   unpaired noisy reps; the A/A control replaced that estimate.

## Caveats

- One workload, one model, one provider's cache pricing (2% cached reads).
  A provider with no prefix caching would show very different numbers.
- 6 reps; per-rep spread is $0.013–$0.034, so only the medians are meaningful.

## In Ollama's own meter (the question that matters)

Ollama returns two prompt fields per call — verified live against
`POST https://ollama.com/api/chat`:

- `prompt_eval_count` — total prompt tokens

# How BabyZilla works

OpenCode v2 gives plugins a hook on compaction and another on every outgoing
request. BabyZilla registers five hooks and one command, and owns zero
OpenCode state — everything lives in `~/.opencode/contextpacks/`.

## The hooks

### 0. `session.hook("context")` — hard per-request budget (Layer 1b)

Layer 1 only runs when OpenCode decides to compact. A model with a 1M-token
window (Kimi K3) may never reach that point, so without this layer the plugin
would have *zero effect* on exactly the long sessions where it matters most.

The `context` hook receives the exact `messages` array about to be sent.
BabyZilla:

1. Estimates the message tokens (`chars / 4`).
2. If the list exceeds the budget — `requestTargetRatio` (8%) of the incoming
   context, floored at `requestMinBudgetTokens` (12K) and capped at
   `requestBudgetTokens` (45K) — compresses, in place, old tool results
   (`result.value` / `output.value` / `state.content`), old assistant text, old
   reasoning (never signed/encrypted) and old image/file attachments.
3. If the request is still over budget, the oldest parts are replaced with
   one-line pointers. Every pointer carries a `babyzilla recall <hash>` handle:
   the exact bytes are in the page store (`~/.opencode/contextpacks/pages/`),
   so paging is reversible for **every** tool, including shell output that
   cannot be re-read from a file.
4. The newest `requestProtectRecent` messages, the newest
   `requestTurnProtectTokens` of the current user turn, the newest result per
   file/command, and every user turn stay verbatim. The protected working set
   is only structurally compressed (head + tail + structural lines) when the
   budget cannot otherwise be met — never blanked or reduced to pointers.
5. A rewrite that would save less than `requestMinSavingsPct` (12%) is rolled
   back, so near-no-op passes do not churn the prompt prefix or the model's
   view of the transcript.
6. Before a part is reduced to a pointer, it is turned into a **ledger row**
   (Layer 3) if it is an old tool step: `#12 · bash · npm test · exit 1 · 3.1K tok
   · recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15`. Tool, target, status and size come from the call
   itself, so the row is a trustworthy index of what was already tried. The
   newest `requestLedgerKeepTokens` (8K) / `requestLedgerKeepRecent` (5) results
   are never ledgered.
7. A **historical** user message above `requestUserBulkMinTokens` (32K) is
   condensed to its opening, its constraint-shaped lines and its closing, plus
   a recall handle. The live user message is never touched — only bulk that a
   harness checkpoint or a pasted transcript left behind.

Every rewrite is idempotent (parts carrying `[ContextPack]` are skipped), and
a failure leaves the messages structurally valid. Measured on a 1.13M-token
Kimi-K3-shaped session: **1,129.6K → 44.9K tokens (96% smaller)**.

The same hook also keeps sessions from growing unbounded: once a request
exceeds `max(proactiveCompactMinTokens, proactiveCompactRatio × model window)`,
BabyZilla calls `ctx.session.compact({ sessionID })` itself (Layer 1c). Without
it, OpenCode waits for ~90% of the window — 900K+ on Kimi K3 — before Layer 1
ever gets a chance to run. Triggers are rate-limited per session
(`proactiveCompactCooldownMs`, 10 min) so a compaction that frees little cannot
loop.

Proactive compaction deliberately waits for a user turn (compacting mid-task
replaces the working set). A long autonomous tool loop never reaches that
boundary, so in stable-prefix mode the cached prompt can keep growing. The
**loop guard** covers that case: after `loopGuardTurns` assistant turns since
the last user message and `loopGuardMinTokens` prompt tokens, it asks for a
queued compaction, rate-limited by `loopGuardCooldownMs`. Set `loopGuard: false`
to allow unbounded tool loops.

### 0b. `session.hook("context")` — grounding: don't guess, verify

A second, independent `context` hook adds one constant system part to every
request:

```
[babyzilla:grounding] Answer truthfully.
- When you are confident, answer directly; do not hedge what you know.
- When you are not certain of a factual claim, say so ("I'm not sure") or verify
  it before asserting it: search, read the file, run the command. Do not ask the
  user to check what you can check yourself.
- Never present a guess as a fact. Label an estimate as an estimate.
- If the user's premise looks wrong, say so instead of going along with it.
```

Three design rules, each for a reason a user would feel:

- **System part, not a prompt edit.** A `prompt`-hook edit becomes the canonical
  *persisted* user turn (OpenCode's own documentation), so the directive would
  live in the transcript forever. `event.system` is assembled per request, so
  this never touches history.
- **Its own hook.** The budget hook above is gated behind `requestCompression`;
  honesty must not disappear because someone turned compression off.
- **Constant bytes.** The same text every request stays in the provider's cached
  prefix. It costs its own ~80 tokens once, then cached tokens.

It is on by default (`grounding: true`) and can be turned off (`grounding:
false`) for work where being wrong out loud is the point — brainstorming, first
drafts. It is an instruction, not a guarantee: it makes verification the cheap
path and a silent guess the exception, and it cannot make a model infallible.

### 0c. `session.hook("context")` — session charter

One more system part on every request: a stable "what this session is" header,
built from the pack's `state` and `decisions` modules plus `index.json`:

```text
[babyzilla:charter] Session memory — distilled at the last compaction and updated only then. Newer turns below outrank it; if a detail you need is not here, read the module files; do not guess.
About: MTG Commander Deck
Snapshot: 2026-10-29
State:
# State
- 78 cards final; proxies allowed
Decisions:
- Removed Wormcoil Engine (illegal)
Superseded: 2 retired facts · inspect: babyzilla memory history
Modules: ~/.opencode/contextpacks/sessions/<sid>/ (index.json lists every path)
```

- **Built from disk, not the live transcript.** The bytes change only at
  compaction, so the header stays in the provider's cached prefix instead of
  busting it on every turn.
- **Capped at 1,200 chars** (`charterMaxChars`): state gets about 60% of the
  room after the fixed lines, decisions the rest.
- **Thin before the first compaction.** A tab with no pack gets `About: <tab
  title>` plus its *first* journal step. The first step is used, not the latest,
  because the journal is append-only: the first one is stable, while "latest"
  would change on every tool call.
- **A snapshot, not an oracle.** The header says newer turns outrank it and
  points at the module files. It prevents losing the beginning of the session;
  it never overrides something fresher in the conversation.
- `babyzilla charter` prints it on demand; `charter: false` disables it
  entirely.

### 1. `session.hook("compaction")` — replace the summary

When OpenCode compacts a session (automatic when the context fills, or manual
`/compact`), the hook receives the full transcript as provider-normalized
messages. Manual and free-tier compactions sometimes pass a single synthetic
message instead; BabyZilla then falls back to `ctx.session.context()` so the
distiller sees the real transcript. It then:

1. Estimates raw tokens (`text.length / 4`). Under `minRawTokens` (4000) it
   yields — native compaction is better than a big pack for small sessions.
2. Pre-trims the transcript to ~48K fed tokens: tool results cut to a 1600-char
   head (results are the bulk), keeping the most recent content intact.
3. Calls `ctx.generate.text` with the **session's model** (or `distillModel`
   if configured) asking for newline-delimited JSON modules — one JSON object
   per line, each self-contained:

   ```json
   {"kind":"state","name":"00-state","triggers":["..."],"content":"..."}
   ```

   JSONL (not one big JSON) is deliberate: truncated output drops only
   trailing lines instead of killing the whole parse. A tolerant line parser
   recovers valid lines from mixed output, with one stricter-instruction
   retry, then a legacy `{"modules":[...]}` fallback.
4. Writes the pack: `<kind>-<name>.md` files + `index.json` (stats, triggers,
   hot flags, `projectDir`) + metadata into OpenCode's compaction message.
5. Sets `event.result` with a compact inline summary (state + decisions
   inlined; cold modules listed by path). This is what the agent actually
   sees sitting at the top of its context.

**Hot/cold policy:** `state` + `decisions` are hot — always inlined into the
summary, never auto-attached (they're already there). `topic`/`code`/`tool` /
`errors` are cold — real files, attached only on trigger match.

**Safety:** every error path yields: no `event.result` → OpenCode runs native
compaction. The transcript is read-only. A result set by an earlier hook is
respected (yield); duplicate compaction events for one session are folded by
a per-session in-flight lock (120s TTL, ownership-tracked cleanup).

### 2. `session.hook("prompt")` — trigger-based module attach

On every user prompt admission, BabyZilla scans the prompt text against each
cold module's trigger words (from `index.json`), plus the cross-session
library for the project. Matching modules are attached as prompt files
(URI `file://…` references), capped by `maxAttach` and
`attachBudgetTokens`. The attached files appear to the agent just like
native prompt attachments.

### 3. `tool.hook("execute.after")` — the journal + tool-result compression

Every tool result appends one line to the session's `journal.jsonl`:
`{t, tool, status, tokens (est), head (≤1200 chars)}`. This is how savings
are quantifiable (`babyzilla stats`, `lowfat pack show`) and how big a session
got before compaction.

The same hook compresses large tool results (Layer 2b, below).

## Layer 2b — tool-result compression (`execute.after`)

Any single tool result whose estimated tokens exceed `toolResultEagerMinTokens`
(default 8000) is compressed at the source — whatever tool produced it:
`read`, `grep`, `glob`, `list`, `shell`, `execute`, MCP tools included — and is
paged through `babyzilla recall` (the original is never deleted), so every
later turn pays the smaller size. Results under the threshold stay inline for
free; `toolResultEagerMinTokens: 0` restores the fixed tool-name allowlist
(`read`, `grep`, `glob` and `list` above `toolResultMinTokens`). The rewrite
keeps a head, a tail, and every structural
(`import`/`export`/`class`/`def`/…), diagnostic (`ERROR`/`FATAL`/`panic`/…) and
`TODO` line; line numbers are preserved and elided spans are marked.

Compression is **deferred by one result**: `toolResultProtectRecent` (default
`1`) keeps the most recent result verbatim, because that is the content the
agent is actively working from. On the next tool call it becomes eligible.

`session.context({sessionID})` returns the live message objects, so the plugin
can compress older parts without touching the session history in the database.
The rewrite is idempotent: a part that already carries the ContextPack footer
is skipped.

## Layer 2 — `execute.before` hook (lowfat integration)

Adapted from the bundled lowfat v2 plugin ([zdk/lowfat](https://github.com/zdk/lowfat),
Apache-2.0). On every shell/bash tool call the plugin asks `lowfat rewrite`
to transform the command (`git` → `lowfat git`, `ls` → `lowfat ls`, piped
`| lowfat` markers are skipped). The rewritten command executes and its
compact output is what the transcript records — plus a row in lowfat's own
SQLite history backing `lowfat stats`.

The lowfat binary is discovered at plugin load: `PATH`, then
`~/.local/bin/lowfat`, `~/.cargo/bin/lowfat`, `/usr/local/bin/lowfat`. If it
is missing, layer 2 logs
`layer 2 skipped: lowfat binary not found` and everything else keeps working.
Install it per `AGENT-INSTALL.md` (release tarball — no Rust toolchain) or
build from source.

## Layer 3 — the turn ledger (`context`, before elision)

Layer 2b compresses a result *once*, at the source. But a 200-step session still
carries those results in every later request. Historically that was handled by
replacing them with a bare pointer, which costs the model its memory of what it
already did.

The ledger keeps the memory and drops the bytes. Each old tool step becomes one
deterministic row:

```
[ContextPack] #12 · bash · npm test · exit 1 · 3.1K tok · recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15
```

Nothing is inferred: the tool name, target (`filePath` / `command` / `pattern`),
exit status, token size and recall handle all come from the call and its result
metadata. No model call, so no drift on every pass.

Rules:

* only steps older than the working set — the newest
  `requestLedgerKeepRecent` (5) results and the newest
  `requestLedgerKeepTokens` (8K) tokens are untouchable;
* nothing under `requestLedgerMinTokens` (60) is ledgered: a row would cost as
  much as the text;
* the newest result per file/command and the current user turn stay verbatim;
* `requestLedger: false` falls back to head+tail and plain pointers.

A row is an *index*, not content. Before editing, re-read the file — the handle
prints the exact original bytes:

```sh
babyzilla recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15        # whole output
babyzilla recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15:120-180 # a span
```

## Token calibration (`babyzilla calibrate`)

Every absolute number here rests on `chars / 4`: the budget floor and cap, the
proactive-compaction threshold, the overflow valve, the savings percentages. That
heuristic is right for English prose and wrong elsewhere — code and JSON carry
more tokens per character, non-English text fewer, and the gap differs per model.

Bundling a real tokenizer was the alternative (`deepseek-recipe`, a model's
`tokenizer.json`). Rejected on three counts: a multi-MB asset, correct for one
model family only, and encoding a 100K-token context on every request costs more
than the compression it guides.

So the plugin *measures* the gap instead of modelling it:

1. **In the request path**, after compression, one ~120-byte line per request goes
   to `calibration/requests.jsonl`: `{at, sid, model, sys, msg, tools, est}`. The
   estimate covers system + messages + tool schemas — the three things providers
   bill as input.
2. **Offline**, `babyzilla calibrate` reads OpenCode's own usage rows
   (`tokens.input + tokens.cache.read`) and pairs them with those lines, one per
   request, by time within the session. An aborted request leaves a gap rather
   than shifting every later sample.
3. **Per model**, the median of `billed / estimated` is stored in
   `calibration.json`, clamped to 0.6–1.8, and only once at least 12 samples back
   it. Fewer than that and nothing is applied — thin evidence must not move a
   threshold.

Samples below 8K estimated tokens, or where messages are less than 40% of the
request, are counted but not used: they measure the system prompt and the tool
schemas, not the messages the budget governs. The report shows how many were
skipped rather than averaging them in.

The factor is applied where a *provider* number is compared with an *estimated*
one — the budget cap and floor, the `requestMinTokens` "don't bother" floor, the
`max(proactiveCompactMinTokens, ratio × window)` trigger, the loop-guard
`loopGuardMinTokens` floor, the overflow valve —
by converting the threshold into estimate space (`estForReal`). Savings
percentages are ratios and cancel out, so they are left alone.

```
$ babyzilla calibrate
  token calibration (chars/4 vs provider billing)
  ────────────────────
  model                                  samples  factor         p25–p90  state
  deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017                    80   ×1.07       1.05–1.18  applied
```

That is the real measurement on this machine: ~7% at the median, 18% at the 90th
percentile (JSON-heavy prompts), and the sample count keeps growing with use. Which is the honest outcome — for this model the
estimate was already close, and the correction is small. The mechanism exists
because the same heuristic is *not* close for CJK text or code-heavy sessions, and
because the factor is per model: a 3× tokenizer difference between two models
should not be invisible.

`--dry` reports without writing; `--reset` deletes the file, and the plugin goes
back to raw `chars/4` on its next 30-second re-read. Disable sampling entirely
with `calibrate: false` (the learned factors still apply).

## Library promotion

Hot modules (`state`, `decisions`) plus cold `tool` and `errors` modules from
real project sessions are **promoted** to
`~/.opencode/contextpacks/library/<project-slug>/` and become attach
candidates in *future* sessions of the same project (e.g. "how we fixed the
ECONNRESET gateway bug" survives session death). The hot flag is preserved, so
with `carryIn: true` a new session's first prompt carries the project's hot
modules over trigger-free, labeled `[carry-in]`, at most once per session (a
`.carryin` stamp under `sessions/<sid>/` prevents repeats). Home-dir and
temp-dir sessions are skipped; promotions are add/merge-only; empty promotions
write nothing. A promoted module whose bytes differ from the library copy first
retires that copy into `library/<slug>/short/` — the same long-term/short-term
rule as a session pack.

## Long-term and short-term memory

Every durable module write goes through one deterministic versioner: a session
compaction, or a library promotion. There are no model calls and no inferred
diffs.

- **Differs** → the old bytes move to `<base>/short/NNNN-<file>` and a row is
  appended to the base's `index.json` under `shortTerm`:
  `{name, kind, seq, at, tokens, path, replacedBy, reason, triggers, hot}`.
- **Identical** → nothing is written, so a no-op compaction creates no history.
- **Dropped** → a module the new pack no longer carries is retired the same
  way, with `replacedBy: null`; "replaced by nothing" is still a fact worth
  keeping.
- **Anchors and `recovered` are not versioned.** They are per-turn snapshots
  and change at every compaction; versioning them would be noise.

`babyzilla memory history` lists the rows (optionally `--session`, `--project`
or `--all`). `babyzilla memory revert <.../short/NNNN-file.md>` copies the old
revision back into the current slot — and the content it replaces is retired
first, so a revert can itself be reverted. The restored module is visible to
the charter and the next prompt immediately, no restart. Retired rows are also
part of `babyzilla memory search` (labeled `short-term`) but they are never
auto-attached: they are backup, not context.

Retention is forever. A revision is 1–3KB on disk; `prune` only removes whole
old session packs, not `short/` rows.

## Memory search

`recall` needs a handle; trigger matching needs the author's keyword. Neither
answers "which session dealt with the ECONNRESET gateway bug?". `babyzilla
memory search <words>` fills that gap by ranking the modules already on disk
with Okapi BM25:

```sh
babyzilla memory search "gateway ECONNRESET"          # open tabs in this workspace
babyzilla memory search "gateway ECONNRESET" --all    # every compacted pack + library
babyzilla memory search "invoice" --project ~/work/shop --limit 3
babyzilla memory search "接続" --json
```

- By default the corpus is the **sessions with an open tab in the current
  workspace**, read from `~/.local/state/opencode/latest/tui/tabs.json`. The
  current OpenCode session (`OPENCODE_SESSION_ID`) selects its own strip, so
  running the CLI from any directory inside that session still finds the six
  tabs; otherwise the longest workspace that contains cwd wins. `--cwd`
  overrides. A missing tab file falls back to all packs.
- `--all` searches every compacted session plus the project library. When the
  search is scoped to open tabs, the library is excluded: its rows do not carry
  a source session, so they cannot be attributed to a tab.
- Raw pages are not indexed: a page is a byte blob with a hash, not a distilled
  fact. A tab that never compacted has no modules, so its `journal.jsonl` rows
  are used as a fallback (tool, status, and the truncated head) — enough to
  find "which tab wrote that file", not the full original. If even the journal
  is empty, the header reports `5 of 6 open sessions` rather than pretending
  otherwise.
- Retired revisions from `short/` are indexed as well, labeled `short-term`
  in the citation. They are backup: searchable, never auto-attached.
- No model, no embeddings, no network, no new dependency. The index is built
  per invocation from the module files, so it cannot go stale.
- Output is capped at 1,200 characters by default (`--max-chars`), one block per
  hit with a citation and a `read` path. `--json` returns the uncapped result
  and the resolved scope (`open` or `all`).
- The command is **on demand**: it costs zero prompt tokens until the model or
  the user runs it. BabyZilla never auto-invokes a search on a prompt.
- The prompt hook's library merge is the other half: when a session has its own
  pack, matching library rows may now replace session rows, but the merged pick
  is capped at the session-only selection's module count and token total. A
  library row cannot enlarge a prompt; if the session had no match, the library
  still contributes nothing (zero would grow to one). Set `library: false` to
  disable the merge.

## Data layout

```
~/.opencode/contextpacks/
├── debug.log                        # plugin log (console.warn is unreliable)
├── calibration.json                 # learned billed/estimated factor per model
├── calibration/requests.jsonl       # one estimate per request (measurement buffer)
├── sessions/<sessionID>/
│   ├── index.json                   # stats, module rows, projectDir, shortTerm history
│   ├── 00-state.md                  # hot
│   ├── decisions-*.md               # hot
│   ├── topic-*.md / code-*.md       # cold
│   ├── errors-*.md / tool-*.md      # cold (+ library-promoted)
│   ├── short/0001-*.md              # retired revisions (never auto-attached)
│   └── journal.jsonl
└── library/<project-slug>/          # cross-session modules: hot state/decisions
                                      # + cold tool/errors, carry-in source
                                      # + short/ retired library copies
```

## Why pointers-first matters

A standard summary says "fixed a bug in the retry logic". A BabyZilla module
says `src/util/retry.ts:40 — the backoff cap was wrong; fixed by <commit>`.
After compaction the agent can read the actual file instead of trusting a
paraphrase. `babyzilla verify` audits these pointers against the current
filesystem (resolving relative paths through projectDir → pack dir → cwd) so
you can see how much of a pack is still live.

## Known limitations

- The charter and every pack module are a **snapshot from the last
  compaction**. Between compactions newer turns outrank the header (it says so
  itself); `/compact` or a lower `proactiveCompactRatio` refreshes it.
- Plugin load is lazy per location; a compaction firing immediately at load
  can be missed (benign — next compaction works).
- Distillation quality depends on the model; very weak models may produce
  thinner modules (still safe — worst case is fallback).
- Windows is untested.

## Maintenance — how to refresh this DB

1. `curl -s https://ollama.com/api/tags | jq '.models[] | {name, capabilities, modified_at}'`
   → ground truth for *which ids exist and their caps*.
2. `curl -s "https://r.jina.ai/https://ollama.com/search?c=cloud"` → one page with
   per-model blurb, usage class, $in/$out, context size, badges.
3. Add new ids to `lib/modeldb.json` (facts). Numbers usually land automatically —
   see below — so only add a `PRICES` row when the id is too new for the cache.
4. Run `node --test test/modeldb.test.mjs` and `babyzilla models --lanes`.

### Where the numbers actually come from

The shipped `PRICES` table is a **fallback**. At load, `hydrateFromOpencodeModels()`
overlays price, context, output limit, and vision/tools/thinking flags from the
`ollama-cloud` block of **OpenCode's own catalog** (`~/.cache/opencode/models.json`)
— the same metadata the host bills against. That is why `babyzilla models` prints
`N model(s) hydrated from OpenCode's catalog`: those entries cannot drift from
what you are charged. Ids missing from the cache (brand-new models) keep the
shipped values and are listed by `catalogCompat()`.

The cache itself can be a stale snapshot: on 2026-10-25 it still listed 7 retired
ids and lacked 5 live ones. Use `/api/tags` to decide *existence*, the cache to
decide *numbers and caps*.

### Proving the table: `babyzilla models --audit`

Recomputes the rate OpenCode *actually charged* per model from its per-request
records and compares it with the table (`ratio`, 1.00 = agreement; tolerance 15%).
This is the drift alarm — run it after a pricing change or a big spend.

The 2026-10-25 run is why the table looks the way it does: it caught DeepSeek rows
priced 2x too high, `mistral-large-4` 2x too low, and `minimax-m3.1-flash` with a
2x-too-high cache rate. Marketing pages say "from $X"; only the bill is truth.

Personal overrides (no upstream edit needed): `~/.config/babyzilla/modeldb.overrides.json`
— a `{ "<id>": { patch... } }` object merged on top of the shipped entries at load.

BabyZilla needs no options to work — defaults are good. Set object-form
options in `opencode.json(c)` (they reach the plugin via `ctx.options` and
hot-reload on config change):

```jsonc

    "babyzilla",                                   // Method A already does this
    {
      "package": "babyzilla",
      "options": {
        "distillModel": null,
        "distillVia": "auto",
        "charter": true,
        "charterMaxChars": 1200,
        "requestCompression": true,
        "requestBudgetTokens": 45000,
        "requestTargetRatio": 0.08,
        "requestMinBudgetTokens": 12000,
        "requestMaxPromptRatio": 0.5,
        "requestProtectTurns": true,
        "requestTurnProtectTokens": 40000,
        "requestMinSavingsPct": 12,
        "requestLedger": true,
        "requestLedgerKeepTokens": 8000,
        "requestLedgerKeepRecent": 5,
        "requestLedgerMinTokens": 60,
        "requestCompressUserBulk": true,
        "requestUserBulkMinTokens": 32000,
        "requestUserKeepTokens": 4000,
        "requestContract": true,
        "distillAnchors": true,
        "distillRecovered": true,
        "evalMaxChars": 400000,
        "distillBudgetTokens": 0,
        "toolResultCompression": true,
        "toolResultEagerTokens": 8000,
        "toolResultProtectRecent": 3,
        "toolResultProtectTurn": true,
        "proactiveCompactRatio": 0.35,
        "proactiveCompactMinTokens": 120000,
        "loopGuard": true,
        "loopGuardTurns": 40,
        "loopGuardMinTokens": 120000,
        "loopGuardCooldownMs": 1800000,
        "maxAttach": 2,
        "attachBudgetTokens": 6000,
        "library": true,
        "carryIn": true,
        "minRawTokens": 4000

    }
```
