
(If both entries exist, the object one wins for options; the plugin loads
once.)

| Option | Default | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toolCompression` | `true` | Layer 2 — rewrite shell commands through the `lowfat` binary before execution (`lowfat` by zdk, bundled integration). Needs the binary; without it the layer is skipped. |
| `requestCompression` | `true` | Layer 1b — the `session.hook("context")` rewrite. In the default `stablePrefix` mode it applies content-addressed compression; with `stablePrefix: false` it enforces a hard per-request token budget. This runs on **every** request, including models whose 1M-token window means native compaction never fires (Kimi K3). Disable only if you want to see the raw history. |
| `stablePrefix` | `true` | Compress each tool result **by its own content**, at the moment the request is built, and never revisit the decision. Because the choice depends only on a part's bytes (and the replacement is a content-hash function of them), an already-sent prefix serialises identically on every later request, so the provider's prompt cache keeps hitting. With position/budget-based rewriting the prefix changed each request and cached input was re-billed at full price — measured on Ollama Cloud: −45% tokens but **+4% credits**. Stable mode measured **−53% credits** on the survey workload, −52% overall. Set `false` to restore the old budget-driven rewriting. |
| `stableMinTokens` | `2000` | Size gate for `stablePrefix`. Results below this stay verbatim: those are the ones an agent acts on immediately, and paging them out buys a recall round-trip. Falls back to `toolResultMinTokens` when unset. |
| `stableOverflowRatio` | `0.9` | In stable mode the budget pass becomes an overflow valve: it only rewrites history when the prompt exceeds this share of the model window. A cache miss is worth paying once to avoid a hard context failure. |
| `distillBudgetDefault` | `16000` | Cap on the transcript fed to one compaction's distiller call when no explicit `distillBudgetTokens` is set and the window is unknown or larger. Small-window models still clamp to 40% of their window. Was 48K — at uncached input price, one compaction of a dump-heavy session billed ~48K tokens on its own, per event. |
| `requestBudgetTokens` | `45000` | Hard max estimated tokens for the outgoing message list (system prompt and tool definitions excluded). Clamped to `requestMaxPromptRatio × model context window`, so a small local model never receives more than it can hold. Lower = more savings, less raw history. |
| `requestTargetRatio` | `0.08` | Aim to keep this fraction of the incoming context (0 = disabled). A 160K-token request is cut to ~13K (>90% smaller); the hard cap wins for 1M-token windows. Set to `0` to only enforce `requestBudgetTokens`. |
| `requestMinBudgetTokens` | `12000` | Floor for the ratio target — never compress a request below this just because the ratio says so. |
| `requestMinTokens` | `20000` | Never apply Layer 1b below this estimated size, even if the budget is smaller. |
| `requestMaxPromptRatio` | `0.5` | Ceiling on one request as a fraction of the model's context window. The window comes from OpenCode's model metadata, so an 8K local model gets ~4K of messages while a 1M model keeps the 45K cap. System prompt and tool schemas are not counted, hence the headroom. |
| `distillBudgetTokens` | `0` | Transcript tokens fed to the distiller. `0` derives it from the model window (40%, capped at 48K); set a number when `distillModel` points at a small-window model. |
| `requestProtectRecent` | `6` | Newest N messages always sent verbatim. |
| `requestProtectTurns` | `true` | Also protect the current user turn's working set: an agentic turn can contain hundreds of tool results, so a message count of 6 covers only a few. |
| `requestTurnProtectTokens` | `40000` | How many tokens of the current turn stay verbatim (capped by the request budget, so small windows still compress). |
| `requestMinSavingsPct` | `12` | Skip a rewrite that saves less than this share of the request. A 2% pass still invalidates the provider's prompt cache and changes what the agent sees; below this threshold nothing is rewritten. |
| `distillAnchors` | `true` | Always keep the last user request and the reply it answers verbatim in the pack, as `00-anchors.md`. Built from the messages, never by the model, so a compaction cannot drop the question the next turn answers. Set to `false` to let the distiller decide. |
| `distillRecovered` | `true` | After the pack is assembled, compare it against the transcript and append a short `00-recovered.md` for facts and `path:line` pointers the distiller left out. Costs one scan of the transcript (skipped above `evalMaxChars`). |
| `evalMaxChars` | `400000` | Longest transcript scanned for `distillRecovered`. Above this the scan is skipped: a multi-MB history costs more to score than the recovered module saves. |
| `requestContract` | `true` | Send the one-time compression contract note (what is paged, what stays verbatim, how `babyzilla recall` works) when a session first compresses. |
| `requestHardProtect` | `2` | If the protected tail alone exceeds the budget, compress it oldest-first but always keep these final N messages. |
| `requestPartMinTokens` | `800` | Parts below this size are not worth rewriting. |
| `requestElideMinTokens` | `200` | In the hard-budget phase, parts are paged down to a pointer once they exceed this size; the page is recoverable via `babyzilla recall`. Lower means closer to the budget, higher means fewer, larger pages. |
| `requestLedger` | `true` | Layer 3. Old tool steps collapse to one deterministic row built from the call itself (`#12 · bash · npm test · exit 1 · 3.1K tok · recall …`). No model call, no drift; the transcript stays an index of what was tried. |
| `requestLedgerKeepTokens` | `8000` | Newest tool results (by tokens) that are never turned into rows. Token-based on purpose: 20 huge reads are still 250K tokens. |
| `requestLedgerKeepRecent` | `5` | Count floor for the same protection, so a few small results always stay verbatim. |
| `requestLedgerMinTokens` | `60` | Results below this size are left alone. |
| `requestCompressUserBulk` | `true` | Condense a *historical* user message above `requestUserBulkMinTokens`: keep its opening, constraint lines and closing, page the rest. The live user message is never touched. |
| `requestUserBulkMinTokens` | `32000` | Threshold for the above. Real instructions are far smaller; harness checkpoints and pasted logs are far larger. |
| `requestUserKeepTokens` | `4000` | Budget for lines that read like constraints (`never`, `always`, `must`, `only`, …) kept verbatim from a condensed user message. |
| `requestElideAttachments` | `true` | Replace old image/file parts with a one-line placeholder (re-attach if needed). |
| `requestElideReasoning` | `true` | Blank old reasoning text. Signed/encrypted reasoning blocks are never touched. |
| `toolResultCompression` | `true` | Layer 2b — compress large `read` / `grep` / `glob` results **at the source**, before they are persisted and resent on every later turn. Keeps the head, the tail, and every structural or diagnostic line; line numbers stay intact so exact ranges remain readable. |
| `toolResultMinTokens` | `4000` | Only tool results above this estimated token count are compressed. Small reads are kept verbatim: compressing them costs more in re-reads than it saves. |
| `toolResultEagerTokens` | `8000` | Layer 2b — when no tool allowlist is configured (or for tools outside it), any single tool result whose estimated tokens exceed this is compressed at the source, whatever tool produced it: `shell` / `execute` / MCP tools included. The result is paged through `babyzilla recall`, never deleted. `0` restores the fixed tool-name allowlist. Small results stay inline — the median tool output is far under this. (Older docs called this `toolResultEagerMinTokens`; that name is still accepted as an alias.) |
| `toolResultHeadLines` | `40` | Verbatim lines kept from the start of a compressed tool result. Any single line longer than ~240 chars is folded (head + fold note + tail) even when kept, and dump-shaped results — minified JSON, bundled JS, one-line command output — fall back to a character window (head ~3K chars / tail ~1.2K chars), so "few huge lines" no longer means "uncompressed". |
| `toolResultTailLines` | `20` | Verbatim lines kept from the end of a compressed tool result. |
| `toolResultProtectRecent` | `3` | Number of most-recent tool results kept **verbatim**. Compression applies to older results only, so the agent keeps working from the content it just fetched instead of re-reading it. |
| `toolResultProtectTurn` | `true` | Never compress results from the current user turn; they become eligible on the next turn. |
| `distillModel` | `null` | `null` = use the session's model. Set `{"providerID":"…","id":"…"}` to pin a specific distiller (recommend a cheap, instruction-reliable model — distillation is a summarization task, not an agentic one). |
| `distillVia` | `"auto"` | How the distillation call is routed. `"auto"` tries the session-less call first and falls back to the session-scoped call when a provider rejects it; when the model's provider is `opencode` (free tier) it starts with the session-scoped call, since the session-less route is always rejected there. `"session"` tries the session-scoped call first. `"text"` keeps the strict legacy behaviour (session-less only, no fallback). |
| `maxAttach` | `2` | Max cold modules auto-attached to one prompt. Raise to 3–4 if you often jump between topics. |
| `attachBudgetTokens` | `6000` | Total estimated-token budget for auto-attached modules per prompt. |
| `library` | `true` | Promote carry kinds (state, decisions, tool, errors) to the cross-session project library. |
| `carryIn` | `false` | Opt-in. On a session's first prompt, attach the project library's hot modules (state, decisions) trigger-free, labeled `[carry-in]`, once per session. |
| `visionRoute` | `true` | Layer 0.5 — when a prompt involves image content (file attachments, concrete image paths, or screenshot wording), send a one-shot synthetic note telling the main model to delegate to the vision subagent with the exact readable paths. Text-only main models see a placeholder instead of the pixels, so routing has to happen before the request. Never routes when the prompt already names the delegate itself. Set `false` to disable. |
| `visionAgent` | `"vision"` | Subagent ID the vision note delegates to. Must exist as a subagent profile (e.g. `~/.config/opencode/agents/vision.md` pinned to a vision-capable model); when the agent catalog is readable and the ID is absent, no note is sent. |
| `grounding` | `true` | Every request carries one constant system part: answer directly when confident, say so or verify with a tool when not, never present a guess as a fact, label estimates as estimates. A system part (not a prompt edit) so it never enters your chat history, and byte-identical each request so it stays in the provider's cached prefix. Set `false` for brainstorming, where being wrong out loud is the point. |
| `charter` | `true` | Every request also carries a stable **session charter**: `About`, the last compaction's state + decisions, a retired-count line, and the pack path. Built from disk so its bytes change only at compaction and stay in the cached prefix. A tab with no pack yet gets a thin title + first-journal-step version. Set `false` to drop the standing orientation. |
| `charterMaxChars` | `1200` | Hard character cap for one charter (~300 tokens). State gets ~60% of the remaining room; decisions the rest. |
| `calibrate` | `true` | Record one `{at, sid, model, sys, msg, tools, est}` line per request so `babyzilla calibrate` can measure how far `chars/4` drifts from provider billing. The learned per-model factor then scales the absolute thresholds (budget cap/floor, proactive compaction trigger, overflow valve) via `estForReal`; savings percentages are ratios and untouched. `false` stops sampling — the learned factors still apply. |
| `minRawTokens` | `4000` | Below this, skip custom distillation and let native compaction run. |
| `proactiveCompaction` | `true` | Layer 1c — ask OpenCode to compact when the context reaches `max(proactiveCompactMinTokens, proactiveCompactRatio × model context window)`. On 1M-token models OpenCode's own threshold is so high that it effectively never fires, so sessions grow unbounded. Set to `false` to let OpenCode decide. |
| `proactiveCompactAtTurnBoundary` | `true` | Only request a proactive compaction when the request starts with a user message. Compacting mid-tool-loop replaces the working set the agent is still using. |
| `proactiveCompactRatio` | `0.35` | Fraction of the model's context window that triggers a proactive compaction. `0.35` compacts a 1M-token Kimi K3 session at ~367K; `0` disables by ratio (the floor still applies). |
| `proactiveCompactMinTokens` | `120000` | Absolute floor for proactive compaction, so small-window models are untouched. |
| `proactiveCompactCooldownMs` | `600000` | Minimum gap between two proactive compactions for the same session. Prevents a `/compact` on every step if a compaction produces little reduction. |
| `loopGuard` | `true` | Mid-loop counterpart to proactive compaction (stable-prefix mode). A long autonomous tool loop never reaches a user turn, so proactive compaction cannot fire and the cached prefix keeps growing. Once the loop is both long and large, ask OpenCode for a queued compaction at most once per cooldown. Set `false` to allow unbounded tool loops. |
| `loopGuardTurns` | `40` | Assistant turns since the last user message required before the loop guard may compact. Lower = fewer tokens, more interruption; higher = fewer compactions, more spend. |
| `loopGuardMinTokens` | `120000` | Prompt-token floor for the loop guard. A long but small loop is left alone; the floor uses the calibrated provider-token scale. |
| `loopGuardCooldownMs` | `1800000` | Minimum gap between two loop-guard compactions for the same session. Prevents a failed or ignored compaction from being requested every step. |
| `selfLearn` | `true` | Self-tuning loop. Per-session telemetry is always recorded (plain file appends, no model calls); when this is on, a cheap analysis call may also propose **one numeric knob change** after `selfLearnSessions` new sessions and `selfLearnIntervalHours` hours. Proposals are applied provisionally, verified by a deterministic replay of the compression pipeline, then kept or reverted. `false` stops the loop but keeps telemetry. |
| `selflearnModel` | `null` | Model for the analysis call. `null` = the session's own model (session-scoped route — free on `opencode`-tier models). Set `{"providerID":"…","id":"…"}` to pin a cheap analyst. Distinct from `distillModel` so the two roles can use different models. |
| `pet` | `true` | Emit desktop-pet events (one small append to `~/.opencode/pet/events.jsonl` per prompt, tool call, compaction and error). `false` disables them; `BABYZILLA_PET=0` does the same without editing config. No effect unless the pet app is installed (`babyzilla pet install`, see [PET.md](PET.md)). |
| `petThoughts` | `true` | Let the pet talk about you: one line per request, reduced locally from the newest assistant reasoning, spoken in **caveman** and pointed at the human ("Human keep ask for bigger pet"). The sentence about the user is preferred over the one about the code; negations, names and numbers are kept. No model call, no tokens, a few seconds on screen, never displacing a spoken line. `"verbatim"` shows the model's own sentence instead; `false` gives a pet that only reacts. Requires `pet`. |
| `selfLearnSessions` | `4` | Finalized sessions (≥3 turns each) of new experience required between two analysis calls. |
| `selfLearnIntervalHours` | `20` | Minimum hours between analyses — loop cadence, not a rate limit. |
| `selfLearnVerifyDays` | `7` | A provisional change runs its acceptance bench at most once per this many days, and never sooner than `selfLearnVerifyGraceHours` after the apply (live signals need time to accumulate). |
| `selfLearnVerifyGraceHours` | `24` | Hours a provisional knob stays bench-free before verification may schedule. |
| `selfLearnKnobs` | `null` | `null` = every knob in the `KNOBS` table below is tunable; an array of knob names restricts the analyst to those. Unknown names are ignored. |

## Self-tuning loop

The loop turns recorded telemetry into bounded, verified knob changes:

1. **Telemetry** — one record per finalized session in `selftune/sessions.jsonl`:
   DB-billed tokens/cost, cache resets, recall counts, duplicate calls, paging
   volume, distill diet. Plus `selftune/recalls.jsonl` (appended by the CLI on
   every actual recall). No model calls, no cost.
2. **Analysis** — after the session + interval gates, one model call receives
   the last 8 session records and the last 10 ledger entries and answers with
   a strict one-line JSON: `{"noop":true,…}` or `{"knob":"…","to":N,…}`.
3. **Apply (provisional)** — numeric knobs only, inside the `KNOBS` clamps,
   ≤ 35% step, allowlist via `selfLearnKnobs`. The change merges into the
   running options immediately and persists in `selftune/state.json`; the
   decision lands in `selftune/ledger.jsonl`.
4. **Verify** — after the grace/throttle windows, `bench/replay.mjs` runs the
   real compression pipeline twice over a fixed transcript: baseline knobs
   versus the proposal. Prompt bytes are a pure function of transcript + knobs,
   so this is exact, free and repeatable (no model calls, no provider noise).
   Kept only if prompt tokens fall, every rewritten result keeps its recall
   handle, already-sent bytes stay byte-identical, the live user ask survives,
   and the knob stays within 35% of its documented default. Fail → revert.
   Every step in the ledger.

   `babyzilla selftune verify --live` runs the dollar bench
   (`bench/ab-live.mjs`, plugin-vs-plugin, spends credits) instead. That one
   measures task quality end-to-end, but on a multi-turn agentic task its A/A
   noise floor can be tens of percent (see `bench/RESULTS.md`), so it is not
   the routine gate. A/A samples only count from marker-complete, work-matched
   reps with both leg orders present; a failed baseline leg defers instead of
   reverting the knob.

Prompts, contract text, model routing, compression algorithms and code are
structurally out of reach — the analyst can only move numbers in this table:

| Knob | Min | Max | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `stableMinTokens` | 800 | 6000 | request-time stable-set floor |
| `toolResultHeadLines` | 10 | 60 | verbatim head of compressed tool results |
| `toolResultTailLines` | 5 | 60 | verbatim tail |
| `toolResultMinTokens` | 1200 | 12000 | compress-at-source threshold |
| `toolResultEagerTokens` | 4000 | 30000 | eager any-tool threshold |
| `distillBudgetDefault` | 8000 | 48000 | transcript budget fed to the distiller — **manual only**: a smaller budget always feeds fewer tokens, but the quality loss is invisible to the replay and too noisy for the dollar bench, so the loop never proposes it |
| `requestMinSavingsPct` | 5 | 30 | per-request rewrite acceptance floor |

Live quality guard: while a knob is provisional, a recall-rate storm
(`≥ max(3, 2.5 × baseline recalls/turn × turns)` recalls in the current
session) triggers an immediate emergency revert without waiting for a bench.

CLI:

```sh
babyzilla selftune status              # state, pending proposal, counts, floor
babyzilla selftune verify              # deterministic replay verdict (free, exact)
babyzilla selftune verify --live [--reps N]  # dollar bench instead (spends credits)
babyzilla selftune noise [--reps N]    # refresh the A/A noise floor (spends credits)
babyzilla selftune revert              # revert the pending proposal manually
babyzilla selftune baseline            # recompute the emergency-revert baseline
babyzilla update [--check] [--yes] [--json]
                                       daily cached update check; asks before
                                       pulling (git checkout only)
babyzilla setup [--yes] [--dry-run] [--check] [--json] [--config PATH]
                                       guided setup: plugin registration and the
                                       permissions BabyZilla needs
```

## Setup wizard

`babyzilla setup` reads the real OpenCode config (`$OPENCODE_CONFIG`, else
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json(c)`, else `~/.opencode/…`), reports what is
missing, and — after showing the exact changes and asking — writes them with a
`.bak-<timestamp>` next to the file.

It can change only these things:

| Change | Why |
|---|---|
| `plugins[]` entry for BabyZilla (or `plugin[]` in the legacy tuple form) | the plugin has to be loaded at all |
| `permission.bash["babyzilla recall *"]`, `…["babyzilla retrieve *"]` = `allow` | paged-out output is only recoverable through these; without it every recall prompts (or is denied) |
| `permission.external_directory["~/.opencode/contextpacks/**"]` = `allow` | lets the agent open a module file by absolute path; packs live outside the project |
| `options.selfLearn`, `options.checkUpdates` | the two switches people actually turn off |

Nothing else is touched. Comments, ordering and formatting survive (the wizard
edits byte spans with `lib/jsonc.mjs`, it does not re-serialize the file), and
the new rules are **appended**, because OpenCode evaluates permission rules
last-match-wins — an allow only wins if it comes after the broad `"*": "ask"`.

If your config uses the newer ordered form (`permissions: [{ action, resource,
effect }]`), the same two rules are appended there instead.

Flags: `--yes` (recommended answers, no prompts), `--dry-run` (print, write
nothing), `--check` (detect + self-test only), `--json` (machine output; never
prompts and never writes without `--yes`), `--config PATH`, `--no-recall`,
`--no-external`.

The self-test actually exercises the install: data-dir write, a compression
round-trip on synthetic output (must shrink and carry a recall handle), a page
write/read round-trip, and a `PATH` check for the CLI. It is offline.

A `deny` is never silently loosened: the wizard keeps it as `"*": "deny"` and
adds only the two narrow allows, and says so in the summary.

Defaults are respected, not assumed: OpenCode allows `bash` when no permission
is configured, so a fresh config needs only the `external_directory` rule (that
one defaults to `ask`). The wizard reports what is *effectively* true — your
action rules first, then a global `"*"` rule, then OpenCode's default — instead
of inventing a gap.

# BabyZilla pet

A 16-bit creature that lives on the bottom edge of your screen, walks around,
and reacts to what OpenCode is doing. 100 expressions, drawn at 64×64 and shown
at 3× by default.

```sh
babyzilla pet install      # build + install the app, copy the sprites, start it
babyzilla pet status       # is it running, how many sprites, last event
babyzilla pet list         # all 100 expressions, grouped
babyzilla pet emit party   # make it react right now (testing / fun)
babyzilla pet gallery      # open the sprite field guide in a browser
```

Requirements: macOS with the Xcode command line tools (`xcode-select --install`)
the first time it builds. After that the app is a normal bundle in
`~/Applications/BabyZillaPet.app`.

## A second pet: packs

A pack is a different look for the same pet — same reactions, same bubbles, same
event bridge, different art. Packs carry whole animations (`idle`, `walk`,
`jump`) instead of one sprite per expression, which is the shape a hand-drawn or
third-party sprite sheet actually has. That is also the only way to get a real
walk cycle: legs can move when a sheet was drawn for it.

```sh
babyzilla pet packs          # what is installed, and which is active
babyzilla pet use lil-dino   # switch, restarts the pet if it was running
```

The same switch is in the pet's right-click menu under **Pet**.

### Choosing a pet: what ships, and the browser

A fresh install wears **Lil Dino** — the pack is part of the plugin, at its own
48px scale, with the caveman voice. The generated art from the first versions is
still copied into the state dir as a fallback (a broken pack should not leave a
blank window), but it is **not** a pet you can pick, and `pet packs` does not
list it.

**Pet → More pets…** opens the browser:

- Every pet in the OpenPets catalog — 1300+ — with search over the names.
- The packs already on disk come first, marked `●` when active and `·` when
  installed; everything else is a catalog entry with its category.
- Picking a catalog pet **installs it** (`pet add`, download + pack conversion)
  and switches to it. `Use pet` or a double-click does that; `Esc` closes.
- The catalog is fetched once and cached for a day. The browser fetches it on
  first open if it is missing, so it works before you have ever run the CLI.

The same in a terminal:

```sh
babyzilla pet catalog --search cat
babyzilla pet add hoodie-cat
babyzilla pet use hoodie-cat
```

The app is a login item, not a shell: it has no `PATH`, so `pet install` pins the
absolute `node` and CLI paths in `~/.opencode/pet/cli.json` and the browser calls
them from there. (The same lesson as the lowfat report, one layer down.)

### Building a pack from a sheet

```sh
node pet/pack.mjs   --sheet ~/Downloads/PACK.png   --name lil-dino --label "Lil Dino"   --cell 32 --crop 4,0,24,24   --rows idle,walk,jump --cols 6 --upscale 2   --out "$HOME/.opencode/pet/packs/lil-dino"
```

- `--cell` is the grid cell in the sheet; `--crop` is the region inside each cell
  that should become the frame (crop out the sheet's margins, once, for all).
- `--rows` names the animations top to bottom; empty cells are skipped.
- `--upscale` is nearest-neighbour, so pixels stay square.
- Frames are copied **cell-relative**, never re-aligned: a jump that rises in
  the sheet still rises in the app.
- `pack.json` records the animations, their frame rate, the canvas size, the
  default scale, and where the art came from.

### Stream Avatars: the sheet's hats come with it

Stream Avatars (on Steam) ships each avatar as a zip: `data.txt` with the cell
size, the animation list **in order** and the per-frame pivot of every gear layer;
one grid sheet where rows are animations and columns are frames; and `gear/`
folders of hats, masks, faces and held items. That is the shape `pet/pack.mjs`
already reads, so one script makes a pack out of it — sprites, walk cycle, and the
dress-up layers with their pivots:

```sh
node pet/import-streamavatars.mjs \
  --zip "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Steam/steamapps/common/Stream Avatars/Contents/premade/littlewalker.zip"

node pet/import-streamavatars.mjs --zip …/premade/*.zip --zip …/StreamingAssets/*.zip
```

- Every avatar in an archive becomes its own pack; `--only littlewalker` picks
  one, `--dir` takes an already-unpacked avatar, and a glob after `--zip` means
  every archive it matched.
- **The pack gets reactions the sheet never drew.** After the sheet's own rows,
  the importer runs `pet/pack-animations.mjs` on the result, which derives eight
  poses from the pack's idle frame (`nod`, `sway`, `shake`, `stretch`, `turn`,
  `lean`, `bounce`, `slump`) and points ~35 expression ids at them. That is what
  turns a seven-row sheet into a pet that leans when it reads and shakes when a
  command fails. `--plain` skips it and keeps the artist's rows alone.
- A row the sheet *did* draw always wins: `block_man`'s real `wave`/`clap`/
  `stomp` answer those expressions, and the derived pose only covers what the
  sheet left out.
- Rows keep the **frame rate the sheet states** (9 for nearly every avatar, up
  to 17 for the fast emotes), and a row the sheet named keeps that name: the
  hero sheets are `custom1`/`custom2` because that is all their labels say, while
  `block_man` has `attack`, `wave`, `hover`, `clap` and `sign_*`. `idle`, `walk`
  and `jump` are never renamed — the app drives those three by name.
- The sheet's own `expressions` come along: an avatar with a `sit` row sits for
  `sit`, `doze` and `bored-waiting` instead of hopping through them, and a named
  `wave`, `clap`, `dance`, `attack`, `stomp`, `spit`, `squat`, `hover` or `sleep`
  row answers exactly that expression. The `sign_up` row is the avatar raising a
  hand, so it answers `tool-question` — the same thing the **?** mark means.
- **Emotes keep the sheet's timing.** `data.txt` states a frame rate, a loop
  count and whether a row holds its last frame; `pack.json` records them per row.
  The app plays one to five cycles (capped at 2.5s) and holds a sign for up to
  2.5s — a wave looped thirty times would otherwise run for fifteen seconds.
- **Paid art stays local.** The importer writes only into
  `~/.opencode/pet/packs`, refuses an `--out` inside the repository, and records
  the licence in `pack.json`: personal use is not redistribution.
- A layer drawn on a bigger canvas than the body — a 48px hair sheet on a 32px
  avatar — hangs off the same ground line, because that is how the artist placed
  it. The pet's window is its own cell, so a layer that reaches past that square
  (a few emotes and chairs) is clipped at the edge rather than making the pet's
  window bigger than the pet.

### Wearing it: hats, masks, held items

A pack built from such a sheet carries a **Wear** submenu in both menus, grouped
the way the sheet's folders are (`Hats`, `Masks`, `Items`, `Hair`, …):

```
Wear  ▸
  Nothing            take everything off
  Hats   ▸  Nothing / Crown / Top hat / …
  Masks  ▸  Nothing / Glasses / Beard / …
```

One layer per group, so a hat and a mask and a held banana can be worn at once.
The choice is `worn` in `config.json` (`{"littlehats": "littlehats/crown"}`);
switching to a pet that never came with that layer drops it instead of persisting
a checkbox that draws nothing. Layers the sheet puts behind the body — backpacks,
chairs, the off hand — are drawn behind it, everything else on top, and the whole
layer flips, bobs and squashes with the pet. A hat that animates by itself (a
flame, a balloon) keeps its own clock while the pet stands still.

**You can see a layer before you commit to it.** Every Wear row carries a small
picture of the item — one cell, trimmed to the ink so a pair of glasses is not a
speck in a 32px field. The importer writes those previews (32px, nearest-
neighbour) so opening the menu never decodes six hundred sheets; a pack from
somewhere else is cropped on the fly. And **pointing at a row previews it on the
pet**: the hat, mask or chair appears immediately, and closing the menu without
clicking puts the old outfit back. Clicking is the only thing that saves.

### Known packs: OpenPet AI Girls

Five anime pets from [AwesomeHou/openpet-ai-girls](https://github.com/AwesomeHou/openpet-ai-girls)
import in one command, each with its own voice:

```sh
node pet/import-openpet.mjs --repo ~/src/openpet-ai-girls
babyzilla pet packs
babyzilla pet use deepseek
```

The importer reads the OpenPet / Codex atlas convention: **8 columns, 9 rows**, one
animation per row, in this order — `idle`, `running-right`, `running-left`,
`waving`, `jumping`, `failed`, `waiting`, `running`, `review`. It crops the character
from the union of its own opaque pixels (a 192x208 cell is not square), box-filters
the frames down to 112px, and maps every expression id onto the body that reads
closest, so a pet with no faces still reacts instead of freezing on idle.

Those girls are not pixel art and their atlas has no faces, so they get movement and
attitude rather than a blink and a grin. The art belongs to its author: the importer
records where it came from in `pack.json` and writes only to
`~/.opencode/pet/packs/`.

### The catalog: 1300+ pets, one at a time

[OpenPets](https://openpets.dev) publishes a catalog of over a thousand pets as
`pet.json` + a 192x208 atlas. BabyZilla can browse it and turn any of them into a
pack:

```sh
babyzilla pet catalog                        # the first 25, + marks what you own
babyzilla pet catalog --search cat           # by name, id or blurb
babyzilla pet catalog --originals            # the 79 made by the OpenPets team
babyzilla pet add hoodie-cat                 # one pet
babyzilla pet add --originals                # all 79 originals (~180 MB of art)
babyzilla pet add --featured --search bot    # or any slice of it
babyzilla pet add https://…/pet.zip          # or a package straight from a URL
```

The list is fetched once and cached for a day in
`~/.opencode/pet/catalog.v3.json`; `--fresh` ignores the cache. A pet is only
downloaded when you ask for it, and nothing is written outside
`~/.opencode/pet/packs/`.

The importer understands both atlas generations: **V1** is the 8x9 sheet, **V2**
adds two rows of look-direction cells that this app has no use for — the crop and
every animation ignore them, so a V2 pet imports exactly like a V1 one. A pet that
only ships SVG is refused with a message rather than guessed at.

**Which voice?** A catalog pet is a stranger: we know its art, not its character.
So each one gets one of four house registers — `chirpy`, `deadpan`, `gruff`,
`regal` — plus `robot` for the machines, chosen from the pet's own id so it always
sounds like itself. The few personalities that are unmistakable are pinned
(`hoodie-cat` is `deadpan`, `luna-techbot` is `robot`). Override any of it:

```sh
babyzilla pet add snoopy --voice chirpy
```

### More faces, without more art

A 15x13 character has far too little identity for a diffusion model to hold: at
low strength it redesigns the creature, at high strength it melts the pose. So
new expressions are authored the way pixel pets always were — on the grid:

```sh
node pet/pack-expressions.mjs --pack ~/.opencode/pet/packs/lil-dino
```

This derives the pack's palette from its own frames, then writes `blink`,
`happy`, `angry`, `surprised` and `hurt` by editing the eye, brow and mouth of the
idle frame, each with a 1px beat so it holds up when looped. It also records an
`expressions` map from every one of the 100 expression ids to the face that
fits — `celebrate` gets the grin, `oops` the X eye, `sleep` the closed one — and
the app plays that face for the duration of the reaction.

At 24x24 the **mouth** carries an expression; a 2x2 eye cannot. So each face
changes the silhouette of the grin (a second open row with teeth, a flat
clenched line, a hole) or adds a brow, rather than nudging the eye. Two faces
were dropped after review instead of shipped: a separate `sleep` was
indistinguishable from `blink`, and a "corner raised" smile read as a flat line.

Because the colours are derived from the pack rather than hardcoded, the same
edits work on any pack that has an ink/shade/light/white relationship, and cannot
silently blank a frame whose palette differs.

Faces are **opt-in**, and one command takes them back out:

```sh
node pet/pack-expressions.mjs --pack ~/.opencode/pet/packs/lil-dino --remove
```

That deletes the face frames, the animations and the `expressions` map and leaves
exactly the animations the pack's artist drew — nothing else in `pack.json` and no
frame is touched. Restart the pet (`babyzilla pet use <name>`) to reload it. A
pack without faces reacts the way it always did: its walk cycle, a jump for
`party`-style events, idle otherwise.

Packs built from someone else's sheet are not ours to redistribute: the builder
writes them to `~/.opencode/pet/packs/`, and the repo ignores
`assets/pet/packs/`.

## What it does

- **Lives on the floor.** It sits above the Dock (`visibleFrame`, not the raw
  screen), wanders, pauses, turns at the edges, and hops. With the built-in art it
  *hops* rather than walks — those front-view sprites have planted legs, so a walk
  cycle can only skate — while a pack that ships a walk gets its own walk cycle.
  Either way the cadence is driven by **distance travelled, not by the clock**:
  one cycle per stride, so the feet can never skate under a body that is not
  moving. If a bubble or a tool call freezes the pet mid-stride, the animation
  freezes with it (it stands and listens) instead of running on the spot.
- **Turns at the wall.** A walk that runs into the screen edge ends at the wall: the
  pet flips to face the room, pauses, then picks somewhere else. Standing at an edge
  with nowhere to go — after a drag, a throw or a pause — it faces inward too, and a
  pet thrown into the edge bounces off it instead of sticking.
- **Reacts.** A prompt makes it listen, a tool call changes its face per tool,
  a **result is read for what it says** (a failing test, a missing file, an empty
  search), every mood it speaks is worn on the body, compaction has it squeezing
  something, an available update makes it hold up a gift.
- **Tells you things.** A pixel-font bubble reports only what matters:
  compaction results, context pressure, tool failures, updates, session
  savings. Everything else is silent, because 30 tool calls should not produce
  30 bubbles.
- **Keeps its mouth shut while you work.** Reactions queue, coalesce, and
  respect `chattiness`.
- **Holds up a mark.** A badge beside its head says what the last turn left for
  you: **✓ done**, **? it asked you something**, **! something broke**. Unlike a
  bubble it never fades — it stays until *you* decide something.

### The status mark

A bubble is an event and fades on its own. A mark is **state**, and the difference
is the whole point: the dino holds up ✓, ? or ! next to its head and keeps holding
it until you act. Answering, fixing, or giving it a new task clears it.

| mark | when it appears | how it is decided |
|---|---|---|
| **✓** done | the turn ended | `session.idle`, and the turn's last words were not a question |
| **?** question | the turn ended on a question | the final answer's last character is `?` |
| **!** error | anything failed | a tool result with an error, or `session.error` / `session.step.failed` |

Rules that keep it honest:

- **A question is read literally.** Only a `?` at the end of the model's own last
  sentence counts (`… right?"` still counts). A question mark in the middle is the
  model thinking, not asking you, and nothing is inferred from tone.
- **An error is immediate and can be withdrawn.** A failed command raises **!** at
  once; a later success in the same turn takes it back down, so a badge left up at
  the end of a turn means "still broken", not "something once went wrong".
- **It survives a restart.** The plugin owns `~/.opencode/pet/mark.json` and the app
  only reads it, so a dino launched tomorrow still holds yesterday's unanswered
  question. One writer, no disagreement.
- **Only your sessions count.** A subagent session going quiet does not raise a
  badge — it is not your turn.
- **It never steals a click.** The badge is a separate click-through window beside
  the head, below

**Variety is structural, not just a long list.** The caveman has eleven asides and
four short grunts per mood (the other voices five and two), and the same machinery
moves between them:

- **Placement.** A short grunt can open the bubble (`Hmph. Parser broken again…`)
  about a third of the time; a longer aside trails it. A thought that already opens
  with a grunt (`Hmm, wait…`) never gets a second one stacked in front of it.
- **Ties rotate.** When two sentences are equally alive, which one is quoted comes
  from the reasoning block as a whole, so two similar steps don't say the same thing.
- **One in nine stays bare.** No aside at all: an aside every single time is a tic,
  not a voice.
- **Mood ≠ silence.** Without mood evidence the dino still speaks, but in a neutral
  register (`Dino note.` `Another rock.`) — it never performs a feeling it cannot
  back up.

A mood is not only written: every thought with one asks the app for the pose that
fits it — angry → `conflict` (the shaking animation), confused → `confused` (a
head-turn), bored → `bored` (a slouch), smug → `proud` (a satisfied sway), teasing →
`tilt-head` — and a `Rawr!` asks for `roar`. A pack without that face maps it to a
derived posture or idle, so the body never freezes to make a point.

**Rawr.** About one thought in twenty-three is a plain `Rawr!` instead of an aside,
in front or behind the thought — deterministic per sentence (so a test can never
flake), unless a caller passes its own `random`. It is deliberately unrelated to the
mood: a dino that only roars when it is cross is a dino you can predict.

The aside is attached so it cannot be clipped away: the thought is clipped to make
room for it, never the other way round. `"petThoughts": "verbatim"` is a quote, so it
gets no tone at all.

Rules that keep it pleasant rather than spammy:

- **one thought per step**, 2.6s throttle, and never the same line twice;
- **speech wins** — a thought never displaces a line the pet is saying, and a
  line arriving mid-thought cuts it short;
- **only the newest** assistant reasoning is used, so a stale thought is never
  replayed later in the turn;
- off with `"petThoughts": false`, `"pet": false`, or `BABYZILLA_PET=0`.

Try it without a session:

```sh
babyzilla pet think "The user wants me to make the pet talk."
babyzilla pet think --caveman "They asked for this twice already."   # explicit
```

## More animations

A pack can answer many states through its `expressions` map, which points an
expression id at an animation name:

```json
"expressions": {
  "thinking": "nod",       "celebrate": "sway",    "compressing": "dash",
  "shell-fail": "shake",   "tool-question": "turn", "tool-task": "stretch",
  "tool-read": "lean",     "tool-edit": "bounce",   "budget-full": "slump"
}
```

`pet/pack-animations.mjs` adds nine of them without repainting anything — the
palette, the pixel blocks and the baseline cannot drift, because every frame comes
either from the artist's own sheet or from the pack's own idle frame. The
Stream Avatars importer runs the eight derived poses itself (pass `--plain` to
skip); for a hand-drawn pack, run it by hand:

```sh
node pet/pack-animations.mjs --pack ~/.opencode/pet/packs/lil-dino \
  --sheet "$HOME/Downloads/PACK - Lil Dino Free/PACK - Lil Dino Free.png" \
  --cell 32 --crop 4,0,24,24 --upscale 2 --row 2 --from-col 6
```

| animation | frames | how it is made | answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dash` | 4 | the sheet row the pack never imported, copied cell-relative | `compressing`, `ship-it`, `self-tune` |
| `nod` | 3 | the body squashing toward its feet | `thinking`, `listening`, `retrieve`, `tool-todo` |
| `sway` | 3 | a shear that leaves the feet planted | `celebrate`, `shell-ok`, `pack-created` |
| `shake` | 4 | the sprite jerking sideways, feet and all | `shell-fail`, `oops`, `conflict`, `offline` |
| `stretch` | 3 | the body growing up from its feet | `tool-task`, `subagent-wait`, `budget-low` |
| `turn` | 4 | squeezed edge-on, then mirrored | `tool-question`, `waiting` |
| `lean` | 4 | tipping forward, feet planted | `tool-read`, `tool-grep`, `tool-list`, `tool-webfetch` |
| `bounce` | 4 | crouch, then a small hop | `tool-edit`, `tool-write`, `tool-bash`, `typing` |
| `slump` | 3 | sagging toward the floor, slowly | `budget-low`, `budget-full` |

The `turn` is the one worth watching: frame 2 squashes the character to a sliver and
frame 3 is the mirror image, so it reads as the dino rotating to face its human —
which is exactly what it should do when the agent needs an answer from you.

`--remove` takes all nine out again and leaves the pack as drawn.

## Removing a pet

`pet install` copies the legacy built-in art into your state dir as a fallback. It
is dead weight once a pack is in place, and it is not a pet you can choose any more:

```sh
babyzilla pet use lil-dino      # you cannot remove what you are wearing
babyzilla pet remove babyzilla  # the legacy art
babyzilla pet remove <pack-id>  # any other pack
```

`remove` refuses to delete the active pet (that would leave a blank window on the
next launch), hides it from `pet packs`, and makes `pet use` say how to get it
back. A later `pet install` does **not** resurrect it — it prints
`skipped babyzilla (removed …)` — because a removal is a decision, not a missing
file. Bringing one back is explicit:

```sh
babyzilla pet restore babyzilla   # or a bundled pack id
```

The art was never far away, just not installed.

Turn it off with the plugin option `"pet": false`, or the environment variable
`BABYZILLA_PET=0`.

## Art pipeline

The sprites are generated and then constrained, not painted:

```sh
node pet/build.mjs master          # 1 reference character
node pet/build.mjs expressions     # 100 faces, conditioned on the reference
node pet/build.mjs locomotion      # 10 walk/run/hop poses, same seed, no reference
node pet/build.mjs sheet           # 10×10 contact sheet for review
node pet/build.mjs data            # pet-data.json for the app
```

- A locked 16-colour palette (`pet/palette.mjs`); every sprite is quantised to it.
- 64×64 canvas, 1px ink outline, bottom-centre baseline so nothing jitters.
- Faces are generated with `--image-path master.png` so the body cannot drift.
- Legs *cannot* move under image conditioning, so locomotion is generated from
  the same seed without a reference — that is the only place the pose is free.
- `pet/manifest.json` records the seed and exact prompt for every sprite, so any
  one can be reproduced.

## Performance

The app idles at 30Hz with a single 192×192 layer and a nearest-neighbour blit;
measure it with `top -pid $(pgrep -f BabyZillaPet)`. It does no network I/O and
writes nothing except its config and, when you move it, its position.

# Example: ledger rows + reversible recall

Layer 3 fires on *old* tool steps of a long session. Instead of a bare
head+tail (or a blind elision marker), each step becomes one deterministic
row built from the call itself: tool, target, exit status, size, and a recall
handle.

Nothing here is invented by a model — every field comes from the tool call and
its result metadata, so the row is safe to trust as an *index* of what was
already tried.

## Measured on a real request

Fixture shaped exactly like OpenCode v2's wire format (assistant `tool-call`
parts + `tool` messages carrying `tool-result` parts), 6 old steps plus the
current one, no model involved:

```
before: 10 010 tok   after: 1 822 tok   saved: 82%   17 messages
```

## What the old steps look like afterwards

```
[ContextPack] #2 · read · src/importer.js · ok · 1.8K tok · recall 1265788f853782f3
[ContextPack] #3 · bash · npm test · exit 1 · 3.1K tok · recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15
[ContextPack] #4 · read · test/parser.test.mjs · ok · 2.4K tok · recall c0a91e5b74f2d318
[ContextPack] #5 · edit · lib/parser.mjs · ok · 1.2K tok · recall 4d7f3e2b90ac5611
```

Read that back and you know exactly where you were: *read the importer, ran the
suite and it failed, read the test, patched the parser*. That is the working
memory a long session actually needs, and it costs ~25 tokens per step instead
of thousands.

## Getting the content back

The handle is a content hash of the exact original bytes:

```sh
babyzilla recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15          # the full `npm test` output
babyzilla recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15:40-80     # just the failing assertions
```

```
$ babyzilla recall 8c1f0b7a9d2e4c15:1-6
# tests 41
# pass 39
# fail 2
not ok 12 - parses nested headers
not ok 17 - keeps CRLF endings
```

Paging, not deletion: the bytes live in
`~/.opencode/contextpacks/pages/<2 hex>/<hash>.txt` and are printed byte for
byte. `babyzilla show <hash>` renders a stored pack, `babyzilla verify` checks
the store.

## What is never ledgered

* the current user turn, in full;
* the newest messages (positional tail) and the newest result per file or
  command — the thing you are about to edit against;
* anything smaller than `requestPartMinTokens` (default 800): it is already
  cheap, and a row would not pay for itself;
* error-bearing results of the *last* turn if they are still in the protected
  window.

The ledger only collapses steps older than the working set, which is exactly
the part a model would otherwise re-read out of habit.

## Tuning

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requestLedger` | `true` | Emit ledger rows for old tool steps. |
| `requestLedgerKeepRecent` | `5` | Newest N tool results are never ledgered. |
| `requestLedgerKeepTokens` | `8000` | …and never the newest N tokens either. |

Turn the ledger off and Layer 2's head+tail (plus elision markers) takes over:

```json
{ "requestLedger": false }
```

See [../docs/OPTIONS.md](../docs/OPTIONS.md) for every knob.

# Scoring a pack: `babyzilla eval`

A pack is a lossy summary, so "did it work?" has an answer you can measure:
take the transcript the pack replaced, pull out the things a continuing agent
would need, and check whether the pack still contains them.

```sh
babyzilla eval                 # newest pack
babyzilla eval <session-id>    # a specific one
babyzilla eval --json          # machine-readable
```

## Real output

A 14-request session, 1.84M raw tokens distilled to a 4.2K-token pack:

```
  pack eval ses_f22c6416affex0OQSkSatVSeN2
  score 24/100 · facts 7/40 (18%) · pointers 3/60 (5%)
  last exchange LOST · 4189 tok (0% of 1842667)
  missing pointers: /Users/sebastian/Downloads/jlpt_n5_simulator.tsx, public/robots.txt, public/sitemap.xml
  missing facts: "Since the file can't be the problem, I removed the failure m" · "Live bytes are identical to local, structurally perfect: no " · "Sitemap could not be read" is actually a different, *more s…
  would append recovered.md (450 tok, 8 lines)
```

That pack is honest but mediocre — it was written by an earlier version that had
no anchors and no gap check. Two of the three findings are the ones users
notice: the last exchange is gone, and 3 of 60 `path:line` pointers the
transcript cited are missing.

## What is measured

| Probe | Where it comes from | Passes when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| facts | long assistant/user sentences in the transcript | ≥60% of the fact's word bigrams appear in the pack |
| pointers | every `path:line` the transcript cited | the pointer string is in the pack verbatim |
| last exchange | the newest user turn + the reply before it | ≥50% overlap for both |

`score = 85% quality + 15% budget`, where quality is
`0.5·factRecall + 0.3·pointerRecall + 0.2·questionKept` and the budget term
rewards staying under 15% of the raw tokens.

The bar is deliberately literal: a pointer the pack dropped is one the agent
will have to re-discover with a `grep`, and a fact it reworded into vagueness
is one it can no longer act on. A pack is not graded on prose quality.

## Two modules the model does not write

Both close gaps the eval finds.

`00-anchors.md` is built from the messages, not by the model: the last request,
the request before it, the reply that answered it, and the names of the tools
used in that reply (never their output). 66 tokens on a real turn, and the
question being answered survives every swap:

```
### The request this pack continues (verbatim)
great, all 3

### The reply it answers (verbatim)
Short answer: no — as code it's the wrong shape for babyzilla…
```

`00-recovered.md` is the eval run at compaction time: if the model's modules
miss pointers or facts that the transcript had, they are appended verbatim to a
hot state module. If nothing is missing, no module is written — the 450-token
append above is the cost, not a constant.

Both are *hot* (always inlined) and both are skipped when the transcript is
larger than 400 000 characters to score, since the scan would cost more than it
recovers.

## Why this and not an embedding index

Vector retrieval answers "which documents are relevant to this query", which
needs a model, a store, and a network call on every request. A pack has to be
built once, locally, deterministically, and be exactly reproducible — the same
transcript must give the same pack. Probes do that; embeddings do not.

# OpenCode v2.0.29 hook/API shapes (empirically verified via debug logs)
- `ctx.session.hook("compaction", cb(event, output))` → return SessionCompactionResult {summary(required), providerState?, metadata?, tokens?}; event ≈ {sessionID, model, messages}.
- compaction event messages are **provider-normalized AI-SDK style**: {role:"user"|"assistant"|"tool", content:[{type:"text"|"reasoning"|"tool-call"|"tool-result", text/output/state}]} — NOT {type:"user", parts:[...]}.
- prompt hook event: {sessionID, messageID, prompt, metadata, delivery}; **prompt is an OBJECT** {text,...}, not an array.
- tool execute.after event: {tool?, input?, result?, status?, sessionID?} — all possibly null; defensive reads.
- `ctx.generate.text({model:{providerID,id}, prompt})` → {text} (used for distillation, ~line 442 of index.js).
- `ctx.session.synthetic` payload requires BOTH name and text (HTTP 400 "Missing key" otherwise).
- `ctx.session.get({sessionID})` → .location.directory (used for library promotion).
- API: `opencode api post /api/session/<sid>/compact -d '{}'` (body required); compaction runs at next step boundary — idle session needs a prompt after; messages route = /api/session/<sid>/context (NOT /messages); OpenAPI at /openapi.json.
- Plugin load is lazy per location → hooks can MISS the 1st compaction registered right after.
- journal.jsonl line schema: {t, tool, status, tokens(est), head(1200 chars)}.

# Design decisions + rationale
- **JS/Node plugin now, Rust deferred** — lowfat Rust source absent locally (~/src, ~/dev, ~/code); user must reveal it before Phase 4.
- **Distiller output = JSONL** (one self-contained JSON object per line): single big JSON object failed on 46.7K-token prompt (GLM-5.2 → "JSON Parse error: Expected '}'"); JSONL truncation drops only trailing modules. Tolerant line parser (recovers any {...}) + legacy {"modules":[...]} fallback; one retry with stricter instruction.
- **Plugin shape**: bare `export default {id:"contextpack", setup:async(ctx)=>{}}`; feature-gate all ctx.* APIs defensively (tool.hook, session.hook fine on v2.0.29).
- **Debug via file** ~/.opencode/contextpacks/debug.log — console.warn doesn't reach ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log under the service.
- **Hot/cold policy**: 00-state + decisions always inlined into summary, never auto-attached (hot); topic/code/tool/errors cold → auto-attached only on prompt trigger match (max 2 modules, 6000-token budget); tool/errors also promoted to library/<project>/ for cross-session reuse (home-dir sessions skipped).
- **minRawTokens=4000**: transcripts below → let native compaction run.
- **Key functions in index.js**: transcriptText, toolBlockText, parseModules, normalizeModel, writeJournal.

# Notable failures during build (all fixed)
- transcriptText extracted `parts` but messages use `content` → tool results (the bulk) vanished; compaction saw 78 tok instead of ~8K. Rewrote extractor.
- Prompt hook bail-guard assumed prompt is array → it's an object; fixed guard.
- 46.7K-token distiller prompt → invalid JSON from GLM-5.2 → safe native fallback (by design); fixed with JSONL + retry.
- `opencode api post .../compact` without body → 400 "Expected object"; /messages route → 404 (correct route is /context).
- First compaction of a live session was missed due to lazy plugin loading; tests used API-triggered compaction after hook registration.
- session.synthetic required unknown keys — discovered via 400 "Missing key" payloads.
